name: jev-proxy
description: jev-proxy is a policy firewall for MCP tool calls: inserted between an MCP client and any stdio server, it allows, denies, or holds each `tools/call` for one-time human approval via ordered rules, with an append-only redacted JSONL audit log.

name: jev-creature-forge
description: Turns natural-language creature descriptions into an inspectable typed genome, using Jev's bounded typed judgments for ambiguous traits while deterministic code derives anatomy, tracks provenance, and renders replayable SVG creatures in a local Studio.

name: jev-cli
description: A command-line client for TypeSafe AI's Jev model that answers typed questions about text—yes/no probabilities, multi-option choices, or scored scales—returning calibrated numbers, JSON output, and gate-based exit codes for branching decisions in shell scripts, CI jobs, and AI agents via MCP.

name: typesafe_sdk
description: TypeSafeSDK is a deprecated Elixir/BEAM SDK (final release 0.4.1) whose TypeSafe API client functionality—authentication, endpoint and model configuration, generated wire operations, and typed response handling—has moved to the provider-neutral `system_one_sdk` successor and `typesafe_api_sdk` provider layer.

name: openjev-sglang
description: FastAPI server exposing the TypeSafe/Jev evaluation API backed by Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on SGLang (Modal-deployable on B200), answering up to 64 Noul/Choice/Score questions per request via single-token logprob readouts over a shared radix-cached prefix.

name: Alloy
description: Alloy is a local skill that applies OpenRouter's "Fusion" method to your installed AI CLIs, dispatching one prompt to a parallel read-only panel (codex, grok, claude, agy) then judging and synthesizing the answers to expose consensus, contradictions, and blind spots.

name: zio-evals
description: A ZIO 2/Scala 3 toolkit for agent evals: run tasks across configurable arms (MCP servers, skills, system prompts, models), grade with generative or binary judges and deterministic checks, and aggregate metrics/transcripts for tests or apps.

name: typesafe-computer-use
description: A macOS computer-use tool that automates GUI interactions for roughly $0.0002 per step by OCR-ing the screen, classifying the next action with TypeSafe, and clicking.

name: jev-browser-qa
description: A Playwright browser-QA toolkit where the fast Jev model answers yes/no and one-of questions to power natural-language assertions, intent-based element picking, and goal-driven click loops, with a JSON CLI, recorded video/traces, and a local run-history dashboard.

name: jevflow
description: JevFlow is a TypeScript library making probabilistic AI judgments (yes/no probabilities, ordinal scores, label choices) typed, provider-agnostic primitives that compose with deterministic threshold workflows to yield explainable, side-effect-free action sets.

name: vercel-jev-mcp
description: A Hono-based remote MCP server deployable to Vercel that relays Bearer-authenticated evaluation calls (jev_ask, jev_classify, jev_score, jev_check) through Vercel AI Gateway to TypeSafe Jev, letting multiple AI clients share one URL without Jev API keys.

name: justmem
description: justmem is a Python CLI that encodes long chat sessions into source-linked memory cards and answers questions via deterministic Jev-guided routing (Lookup/Compose/Replay), embedding retrieval, reranking, and cited evidence-grounded answers, with an offline mode for tests.

name: dasheng
description: A Next.js read-aloud trainer that streams microphone audio through Confucius4-R2T2 ASR, aligns recognized words to the target text, asks Jev closed-form questions to flag and classify mismatches, and computes local fluency/completeness scores—with mock mode for offline demos.

name: jevernetes
description: Jevernetes live-tails Kubernetes logs via kubectl into a terminal or localhost dashboard where TypeSafe Jev semantic analysis (or offline keyword rules) flags anomalies, groups repeats, and lets you inspect context, suppress expected events, and copy evidence to coding agents.

name: visual-jev
description: A local, image-native typed-decision tool on a Qwen3-VL backbone that returns calibrated numerical distributions for choice, score, and noul questions over images—without generating text—via packed question branches, a learned pointer head, and fail-closed checkpoint loading.

name: jev-explained
description: jev-explained is a tool that provides explanations of Jev, helping users quickly understand what it is and how it works without digging through external documentation.

name: jev-review-action
description: A GitHub Action that reviews pull requests or catalog submissions by collecting bounded repository evidence, querying the TypeSafe Jev typed-judgment model via a provider fallback chain, applying a maintainer-defined JSON policy, and posting one updatable advisory PR comment.

name: doom-jev
description: An autonomous ViZDoom agent that couples Doom's 35-tick engine with async ~10 Hz Jev SystemOne inference, using geometric raycasting, line-of-sight target filtering, hybrid macro/micro actuation, and a Rich terminal HUD for stutter-free real-time play.

name: jev-lead-scorer
description: A dependency-free Python toolkit that scores sales leads via Jev's typed AI primitives (fit score, outreach angle, skip flag with confidence), then logs sends, replies, and bookings in SQLite so a per-variant funnel reveals which opener actually books meetings.

name: polar_llama
description: Polar Llama is a Python library that runs parallel LLM inference (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Bedrock) directly on Polars dataframe columns, adding structured Pydantic outputs, tool calling, prompt caching, checkpointing, per-row cost tracking, and vector search.

name: jev-go
description: jev-go is an unofficial, standard-library-only Go client (Go 1.26+, Apache-2.0) for TypeSafe's System One API that returns typed answers—Noul probabilities, Choice categories, and Score scale ratings—with explicit configuration, injectable HTTP clients, optional retries and request-size caps, plus a PR-triage CLI example.

name: jev-tetris
description: jev-tetris is a dependency-free Node.js app that pits TypeSafe's Jev model against Claude Haiku or Gemini Flash in real-time versus Tetris—shared seeded pieces, rising gravity, garbage rows for cleared lines—plus human-vs-Jev and solo modes with per-move stats, latency, and cost tracking.

name: codex-context-diet
description: A Codex plugin whose PostToolUse hook sends bulky tool results to TypeSafe's Jev for keep-or-drop verdicts, replacing stale output with a truncated head plus a one-line note so long sessions stop re-sending dead weight on every request.

name: reflex-gate
description: ReflexGate is a Windows desktop gateway that wraps a local Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B model on llama.cpp into a sub-second HTTP server (127.0.0.1:8090) providing agent-loop endpoints for stop-condition gating, error/status extraction, secret and prompt-injection scanning, and typed yes/no or choice decisions—eliminating cloud latency and token costs for autonomous agent iteration.

name: jev-cli
description: jev-cli (`jev`, npm package `jevctl`) wraps TypeSafe's Jev model to return fast, cheap probabilistic judgments—verify claims, screen for prompt injection, classify, extract, rerank, match, route—via scriptable commands with JSON output and exit codes for gating CI.

name: jevarena
description: JevArena is an open-source web arena for blind head-to-head judging that pits the Jev judge against any OpenRouter model on user-submitted questions, revealing model identity, latency, cost, and confidence only after voting, while keeping API keys in browser memory and including a reproducible Python benchmark harness (JevJudge-Bench) built on pinned JudgeBench, RM-Bench, and RewardBench 2 data.

name: JevEmon
description: JevEmon walks a real Pokémon FireRed ROM by reading overworld state from RAM, offering the LLM typed choices of reachable destinations and legal battle moves, then pathing and pressing buttons to execute its decisions — handling wild encounters and re-planning from wherever they end, verified from the Player's House through Pallet Town to Viridian City.

name: seen
description: Seen is a macOS menu bar app that continuously captures your screens and windows, OCRs their text locally with Apple's Vision framework, and lets you search that visual history from anywhere via Shift-Command-Space — optionally ranking results with the Jev model through your own TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway key.

name: JevFind
description: JevFind is a Rust CLI for semantic code search that turns plain-English queries into ranked file matches with line ranges and confidence scores by filtering paths by relevance, scanning bounded code windows via the TypeSafe API, and supporting tunable thresholds, parallelism, retries, and a live debug tree.

name: hermes-jev-plugin
description: A Hermes Agent plugin exposing TypeSafe Jev’s calibrated Noul/Choice/Score judgments as four tools—jev_evaluate, jev_check, jev_route, jev_score—for batched atomic decisions, failure triage, review gates, task routing, and severity scoring in coding-agent workflows, plus a bundled question-design skill.

name: semcheck
description: semcheck is a Go linter whose rules are plain-English yes/no questions—AST matchers pick nodes, a pluggable decision model judges each fragment with type-checker context—so semantic checks like "does this log call leak PII" work via CLI, go vet, or golangci-lint.

name: AskJev
description: AskJev is an MCP server and optional browser extension that lets Claude Desktop drive Brave/Chrome via CDP from plain-English goals, with TypeSafe Jev making on-page action decisions and a Guard freezing irreversible clicks (pay, delete, send, publish) at risk ≥ 0.65.

name: jev-playground
description: An interactive playground of eight widgets for learning TypeSafe's Jev model, which answers typed choice, score, and boolean questions over given state with directly usable probabilities, showing raw request/response, latency, and cost for routing, triage, scoring, agent, and guardrail experiments.

name: commentcop
description: Commentcop is a CLI that uses TypeSafe's Jev to score JS/TS code comments for accuracy and usefulness out of 100, ranking the weakest first while respecting `.gitignore`, skipping generated code and dependencies, and offering dry-run previews, ignore files, and cost estimates to help prioritize comment review.

name: jevspire
description: JevSpire is a dependency-free Node 22+ external player that drives Slay the Spire via CommunicationMod's stdin/stdout JSON protocol, translating each game snapshot into a validated action list sent to an OpenRouter LLM (or Jev's decisions endpoint), with per-request prompts, a 24KB payload cap, action limits, auto-pause on unsupported screens, and JSONL run logs for debugging.

name: parallelConstraintDecoding
description: A constrained-decoding engine (Java FFM bindings to llama.cpp, plus a Python/MLX reference port) that fills an entire JSON schema of booleans and enums in two forward passes instead of token-by-token generation, yielding schema-valid-by-construction output with per-field calibrated confidence, benchmarked ~8-18× faster, and demoed via a local web app.

name: rizzo-flow
description: Rizzo Flow is an open-source local llama.cpp server that turns unstructured state into typed probabilistic decisions—booleans, choices, scores, numbers—by reading answer-letter logits rather than generating tokens, with a Jev-compatible HTTP API.

name: jev-mcp
description: jev-mcp is an MCP server that returns typed judgments — classification labels, rubric scores, yes/no checks, and abstaining candidate matches — over a closed answer set in ~130 ms with no text generation, exposing seven tools, calibrated confidence distributions, and a ~95% agreement rate on clean labels.

name: pi-heed
description: pi-heed is a runtime guardrail for the pi coding agent that checks each side-effecting tool call against the user's conversational permissions and prohibitions, keeping structured policy state—including exceptions, lifts, and temporary grants—that survives context compaction.

name: jev-lexer
description: An experimental language-agnostic syntax highlighter that mechanically splits source into words and symbols, classifies each part via paid Jev LLM queries into nine visual classes, and emits Shiki-compatible tokens, HTML, or ANSI — useful mainly as a measured cost-vs-accuracy experiment, not production tooling.

name: typesafe-mcp
description: An MCP server that exposes TypeSafe Jev's typed decision engine (choice, score, and noul verdicts with probabilities) as a single `evaluate(state, questions)` tool, with built-in guidance for batching, atomic questions, and confidence gating, installable via npx with a TypeSafe API key.

name: jev-minecraft-factory-sorter
description: An anonymously accessible React 19/Canvas 2D Minecraft factory simulator and Express 5 backend for spawning, tossing, inspecting, and routing 429 vanilla/modded blocks through TypeSafe Jev, with server-side credential handling plus cache, latency, cost, and health accounting.

name: pi-stuff
description: A monorepo of seven pi agent extensions that add TypeSafe risk-scored bash auto-approval, live context-window usage charts and status widgets, a Codex usage meter, persistent self-continuing goals, ANSI-free bash output, and encrypted server-side compaction.

name: jevall
description: JEVALL is an inference gateway that turns multimodal language models into constrained decision services, answering typed choice/score/noul questions via one batched backbone pass and candidate-label softmax to return stable labels, probabilities, and latency diagnostics for controlled production workflows.

name: a0-typesafe-ai
description: Agent Zero plugin adding a `typesafe_query` tool that asks Jev typed Choice, Noul, and Score questions over shared evidence in one call, returning probability cards with distributions, token counts, and raw JSON via the official TypeSafe Python SDK.

name: mario-jev
description: A uv-managed Python prototype that plays NES Super Mario Bros. by pausing the emulator, sending decoded RAM state to a Jev model for focused movement/jump decisions, composing answers into controller inputs, and logging decisions, with scripted, replay, and headless modes.

name: jevvy
description: Jevvy is a local Next.js playground for exercising TypeSafe AI decisions—compose a shared state with Choice, Score, and Noul questions, run them live with your own API key, and inspect typed answers—plus an arcade where Jev pilots a space shooter from text radar.

name: jev-mobile
description: jev-mobile is a durable Android automation sub-agent that turns high-level tasks into safe, verified USB-device operations by persisting work in SQLite and looping observe→normalize→decide→mutate→verify with TypeSafe Jev choosing only prevalidated semantic actions.

name: dehydrator
description: Dehydrator is a Python library that wraps Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible LLM clients to replace large tool lists with a single `tool_search` tool, performing client-side BM25 and/or Jev-based semantic search (including MCP tools) so only matched tools are sent, and it can also run as an MCP gateway server.

name: pg-jev
description: pg-jev is a PostgreSQL extension that lets you filter, rank, and classify table rows with plain-language conditions via SQL functions (`jev`, `jev_prob`, `jev_score`, `jev_choice`) backed by TypeSafe's Jev model, which returns calibrated probabilities per row—using batched API requests, read-ahead streaming, and session caching—without indexes or embeddings.

name: pi-jev-guard
description: Pi extension that pre-reviews proposed code edits against Markdown-defined rules via the TypeSafe Jev API, reporting each violation's exact rule text and source line range, with an enforcement mode that blocks noncompliant writes within the configured repository scope.

name: jev-go
description: Go SDK for TypeSafe's Jev API that provides a client (configured via `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or functional options for API key, HTTP client, and base URL) to submit `SystemOne` evaluation requests with `NoulQuestion`, `ChoiceQuestion`, and `ScoreQuestion` types returning matching typed answers, surfacing non-2xx responses as `*APIError` with status, headers, and body for caller-managed retry logic.

name: jev-triage
description: A dependency-free Go CLI that batch-triages text messages through TypeSafe AI's Jev decision API—returning typed category, urgency score, and frustration probability per message in parallel requests—then prints an urgency-sorted table, routes low-confidence items to a manual-review list, and writes an HTML report.

name: wellposed
description: wellposed is a zero-dependency CLI and agent skill that lints TypeSafe jev requests against 35 structural rules (broken references, missing "none of the above" options, oversized data), adds optional jev-based semantic checks, and self-scores against a labelled corpus.

name: cultivar
description: Cultivar is a CLI tool for testing agent skills against YAML-defined tasks, running evals locally or in isolated Modal sandboxes across Claude, Copilot, and Gemini runners, grading results against criteria, and iterating via traces, benchmarks, and parallel repeats.

name: jev-security-scan
description: A Python 3.10+ CLI and Agent skill that statically audits Agent Skills, MCP configs and source code before installation or execution, combining offline pattern checks with optional TypeSafe Jev model analysis to flag prompt injection, credential theft, exfiltration, and supply-chain risks with file/line evidence, verdicts, exit codes, and explicit coverage gaps.

name: jev-usher
description: jev-usher is a preview-stage CLI, Claude Code plugin, and TypeScript library that uses TypeSafe's JEV model to route launch prompts to a suitable Claude model tier and selectively filter noisy tool output within budgets while preserving originals for recovery, reducing context size without losing the ability to restore filtered content.

name: pi-typesafe
description: Pi extension exposing TypeSafe's Jev judgment model as a `typesafe_evaluate` tool returning calibrated probabilities for batched choice/score/noul questions, plus terminal test/playground commands and a typed client API with shared auth, spend tracking, and daily budget caps.

name: jev-pii-guardrail
description: A UiPath prior-authorization triage agent whose TypeSafe Jev guardrail scores each model boundary for per-type PII probability and patient identifiability, logging detections fail-open without masking or blocking, plus Action Center escalation and a reviewer-note return loop.

name: pi-jev-sentinel
description: A guard for coding agents that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to judge each tool call's intent and risk, screen tool outputs for prompt injection, and check finished replies—shipping as a Pi extension and as Claude Code/Codex CLI hooks, with secret scrubbing.

name: jev-go
description: A Go client for TypeSafe's Jev model that returns typed judgments—yes/no probabilities, option distributions, and weighted scores—instead of generated text, with parallel question batteries, concurrent batching, retries, and typed errors so application code keeps policy and thresholds.

name: jev-codex-workbench
description: A Codex plugin that gates Jev semantic judgments—routing, ranking, triage, verification—behind a local no-network policy classifier and expiring workspace-scoped grants, reducing unnecessary context expansion while keeping Jev output untrusted and unable to authorize actions.

name: TypeSafe
description: TypeSafe is a SwiftPM client for the TypeSafe System One API mirroring the official JavaScript SDK, letting Swift code ask typed noul, choice, and score questions and decode structured answers via an async client configured with TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

name: jevmeter
description: jevmeter is a CLI that gives any video a live BS meter: it transcribes speech, scores every sentence with Jev's calibrated yes/no probabilities via presets (debate, earnings call, podcast, sales pitch) or custom JSON questions, flags dodges, and renders a postable 16:9 edit with highlights, hyperlapse, and scoreboards.

name: python-jev-if
description: A Python helper (`jev_if.py`) exposing `jev()` and `jev_probability()` functions that let ordinary `if` statements branch on yes/no natural-language questions about JSON-serializable `state` data, using TypeSafe's Jev/Noul API with a configurable probability threshold (default 0.5), selectable model, exception-based error handling, and mock-driven tests that run without an API key.

name: typesafe-sdk-rust
description: Rust client for the TypeSafe AI API that sends named questions (noul, choice, or score) about a state payload to System One and returns typed answers, with a typestated builder, configurable retries and timeouts, async/blocking modes, and Python SDK 0.6.0 parity.

name: jev-pruner
description: A Claude Code plugin that runs TypeSafe's Jev on Bash stdout exceeding ~10,000 estimated tokens, scoring line-chunks against session history to omit noise as `[N lines omitted]` markers while preserving diagnostics, whole documents, and a full-output archive—reducing context carried into later turns without summarizing.

name: jeff
description: jeff is a self-hosted implementation of TypeSafe's jev System One API powered by the 400M-parameter GLiFormer model, serving SDK-compatible choice, score, and noul classification endpoints more cheaply than jev, though less accurately on reasoning-heavy tasks.

name: jev-leftpad
description: jev-leftpad is a satirical Node.js 20+ package that left-pads a value by sending one non-retried TypeSafe API request per call, where the "Jev" model picks among criteria `space_0`–`space_10` to decide how many spaces (max 10) JavaScript prepends—a costly, failure-prone alternative to `padStart()` not meant for production.

name: hunk-triage
description: A hunk extension that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to reorder changed files into review-priority groups—core, supporting, tests, fixtures, docs, config, mechanical, generated—using commit or pull-request context, with caching and configurable model, timeout, and threshold settings.

name: typesafe-sdk-swift
description: TypeSafe AI Swift SDK is a dependency-free Swift 6 client for the TypeSafe AI API supporting macOS/iOS/tvOS/watchOS, offering typed SystemOne questions, model listing, retries, cancellation, injectable transports, and backend-proxy or direct API-key authentication.

name: jev-judge
description: Turns a structured legal case record (facts, evidence, arguments, law, precedents) into a probabilistic ruling—prevailing party, remedy, findings, strength scores—with calibrated confidence, via a one-case UI or resumable batch CLI scored against real outcomes.

name: jevmoji
description: Jevmoji is a Cloudflare Worker + Vite web app that scores up to 40 characters of input text against a generated Unicode emoji catalog using TypeSafe's Jev model, returning many ranked emoji matches alongside a keyword-based local "hits" shortlist while keeping the API key server-side.

name: jevinize
description: A Claude Code skill that transforms a described use case into a working classifier/router system powered by simple-jev, scaffolding the routing logic that directs inputs to the appropriate handler.

name: typesafe-sdk-python
description: Python SDK for TypeSafe AI that installs via `uv add typesafe-sdk` and provides a `TypeSafeClient` (authenticated via `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) whose `system_one` method classifies input state into structured `Choice` categories defined by instructions and criteria, returning typed results.

name: jevlint
description: jevlint is a concurrent Jev-backed semantic linter that lints files matched by configurable rule sets against Markdown-defined rules with error/warning severities, caching each verdict, localizing violating lines, and streaming watch-mode JSON diagnostics for its bundled VS Code extension.

name: jev-preflight
description: A Claude Code plugin that snapshots a private Git baseline each turn and sends the redacted diff to TypeSafe's Jev API, scoring eight risk axes so high-risk changes get one focused re-investigation before finishing, while failing open on errors.

name: jev-langfuse-trial
description: A Python harness that runs Jev semantic-correctness signals into a GPT-4o Langfuse managed evaluator, supports paired Jev-enabled/Jev-disabled runs and a 10-case benchmark, and records traces and scores for comparing semantic-equivalence judgments.

name: gavel
description: An OpenClaw plugin exposing a `jev_decide` tool that lets agents make structured decisions — probabilities, option picks, and rubric scores with calibrated confidence — via TypeSafe's Jev model on OpenRouter in ~200ms for ~$0.00002, replacing slower, costlier LLM calls.

name: jev-comment-triage
description: A WordPress plugin that auto-moderates comments with the TypeSafe Jev model—scoring spam, scam/phishing, and toxicity in an asynchronous per-minute WP-Cron drain that approves, spams, or holds comments without blocking submission or overriding the site's own moderation policy.

name: TiVM
description: TiVM is a computer-use test agent that drives a disposable Dockerized Linux desktop, perceiving apps via the AT-SPI accessibility tree, planning with GPT or TypeSafe Jev, acting through a11y invoke or xdotool, and exporting verdicts, timelines, and videos per run.

name: discern
description: Discern is an Effect v4 library that batches provider-neutral `DecisionModel` judgments (classifications, probabilities, ratings) into type-safe pattern-matching policies and routable procedures, treating uncertain model output as an explicit branch instead of silently rounding it away.

name: jev-rules
description: A Claude Code plugin that asks the Jev decision model, per prompt and per edited file, which of a project's Markdown rules and codebase-map documents apply, injecting only the matches in under a second and failing open to all rules on any error.

name: jev-eval-agent
description: A benchmark agent with 100 mocked tools (eve + OpenRouter) that measures the steps, calls, tokens, and efficiency needed to finish 6 tasks when the LLM picks tools itself versus when TypeSafe's Jev classifier routes each step, with a results dashboard.

name: jev-ultrafast
description: jev-ultrafast is a browser-use tool built for maximum speed, providing ultra-fast browser operations when execution latency is the priority.

name: jev-tweet-radar
description: A Chrome MV3 extension that scores each X timeline post and your drafts with one Jev (TypeSafe System One) API call, showing calibrated probabilities for engagement-worthiness and tags like spam/buzz/AI-ish, with goal-aware judging, opacity-based timeline filtering, reply-context scoring, and per-day cost tracking.

name: nimble
description: Nimble scores text against a flat schema of enum and boolean questions, returning the chosen answer and per-candidate probabilities from a single forward pass without generating reasoning, and provides the contrastive data-curation and LoRA fine-tuning recipe for its 9B model.

name: swift-typesafe
description: Swift 6.4 SDK for TypeSafe AI mirroring the Python 0.7.0 API, providing macro-generated typed and runtime-dynamic question schemas, retry/backoff policies, typed errors, swift-log logging with credential redaction, and pluggable HTTP transports on Apple platforms and Linux.

name: jev-spring-boot-bookstore
description: A Spring Boot 4 bookstore API demonstrating TypeSafe Jev via jev-spring-boot-starter for automated genre/audience tagging, review moderation with sentiment and inferred ratings, and natural-language recommendations atop Spring MVC, JPA, and seeded H2.

name: bonsai-decision-engine
description: A tool that runs the 5.95 GB ternary Bonsai 2 27B as a generation-free typed decision model on one RTX 4060 8GB, returning calibrated probabilities over declared options (192/231 public231, ECE 0.037) via local API, CLI, and Python client.

name: open-jev
description: openjev is a CLI and HTTP server that scores pre-written options against a context using a local Gemma 3 4B on Apple silicon via MLX — prefill once, batch-score all options in one forward pass — with normalization modes, a TypeSafe System One-compatible API, evals, benchmarks, and trainable heads on frozen features.

name: ulka
description: Ulka is an experimental local Chromium extension combining FX planning, Jev action selection, Vercel AI Gateway models, accessibility-tree observation, approvals, evidence capture, and Stagehand-style observe/act/extract primitives for supervised browser automation.

name: mysql-ailike
description: A native MySQL plugin that adds an `AILIKE` operator and `ailike()` function for filtering rows and comparing text columns against natural-language conditions, enabling semantic search and relationship-based joins evaluated via TypeSafe API calls.

name: Qwansh
description: Qwansh is a local discriminative Transformer decision model that encodes a shared state once, scores all caller-supplied answer candidates in a single batched pass, and returns schema-valid probability distributions for yes/no, multi-choice, and ordinal-score questions.

name: jev-reflex-autonomy-lab
description: An interactive multi-drone autonomy simulation where 1–15 drones steer via TypeSafe Jev System 1 reflexes that can asynchronously consult an optional OpenRouter System 2 planner when confidence drops, with seeded scenarios, per-drone telemetry, latency/confidence charts, and JSON export for comparing solo reflexes against guided flight.

name: ask-jev
description: Ask Jev provides an AskJev CLI, Dockerized stdio MCP server, and Astra skills that submit typed Noul, Choice, and Score checks to TypeSafe, letting agents validate interpretations, plans, edits, analyses, tool results, and completion claims against evidence during ongoing work.

name: jev-cli
description: jev-cli is a Python-stdlib CLI and pi extension that turns program or business state descriptions into structured Jev decisions—binary probabilities, option choices, or scores—for routing, classification, urgency gating, and workflow gates via TypeSafe direct or OpenRouter.

name: jev-doom
description: jev-doom runs the Jev model in real Freedoom via ViZDoom, with a local dashboard showing game frames, choices, probabilities, navigation, latency and cost, editable standing orders, a persistent $15 spend cap, and TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway providers.

name: jarviscore-framework
description: JarvisCore is an Apache-2.0 Python runtime for multi-agent systems: agents discover each other over a SWIM gossip mesh, claim crash-durable workflow steps from Redis (surviving `kill -9`), and invoke 150+ services through a zero-trust credential vault — no central orchestrator.

name: laya-vs-jev
description: An Apple Silicon tool that races a local MLX typed-decision model (Laya) against TypeSafe's hosted API model (Jev) in Chrome's T-Rex game, with live latency charts, safety overrides, crash replays, and 1080p run export for comparing on-device versus cloud inference.

name: jev-mailroom
description: jev-mailroom is a local read-only mail-triage PoC: .eml fixtures feed a fake IMAP server, a listener gets 11 typed Jev answers per email in one call, Python rules assign kind/category or review, and a no-build dashboard polls results.jsonl.

name: jev-clinical-trial-prototype
description: Local web app that screens ~500 synthetic clinical notes against editable trial criteria via TypeSafe's Jev model, streaming per-note results over SSE with hash-based caching, confidence-slider re-rolls, flip tracking, calibration eval, and Claude-compiled criteria.

name: jev-oas-sentinel
description: A CLI tool and GitHub Action that compares two OpenAPI documents to catch behavioral breaking changes—combining deterministic structural diff checks (removed operations, required parameters, enum narrowing) with probabilistic semantic evaluation of changed descriptions, defaults, retries, ordering, pagination, authorization, and error semantics, producing pass/review/block verdicts with SARIF, J

name: progressgate
description: ProgressGate is a TypeScript SDK that supervises agent trajectories via TypeSafe Jev semantic signals and a deterministic policy, detecting when differing actions repeat the same contradicted assumption and returning CONTINUE/WARN/REPLAN/HALT decisions with fail-open defaults to stop wasteful spinning without naïve step counters.

name: jev-workflow
description: jev-workflow is a TypeScript library that drives iterative workflows by having the Jev model pick the next action from a described set, while the application owns state, supplies only decision-relevant facts, executes chosen actions, and calls `update()` to continue as state changes.

name: pi-jev-context
description: pi-jev-context is an opt-in, reversible Pi extension that sends session history to the TypeSafe Jev judgment service to score older messages for relevance, hiding low-scoring tool exchanges and assistant text from future model context—without deleting them—via configurable threshold, protected buffer, branch-aware caching, and `/jev` commands.

name: smart-switch
description: SmartSwitch is a macOS menu-bar window switcher that, on ⌘`, sends your recent app-switching history (dwell times, time of day, last 10 manual ⌘Tab switches) to TypeSafe's Jev model to predict and activate the most likely next window, falling back to the last-used app on failure or 1 s timeout.

name: Canny
description: Canny is a hook-based warden for Claude Code and Codex CLI that records an append-only ledger of agent actions, blocks "done" claims until a test, build, lint, or type-check passes after the last code edit, denies secret-shaped writes and test-removal edits, and optionally asks Jev for calibrated judgments that can only relax—never harden—its deterministic gates.

name: decio
description: Decio is a Unix-friendly CLI that turns piped or configured context into typed choice, boolean, or score decisions via an API provider, optionally dispatching only pre-declared trusted actions so scripts, hooks, CI/CD, and agents can automate decisions without executing model-generated commands.

name: jev-pii-checker
description: jev-pii-checker is a CLI that scans stdin/files for PII using TypeSafe's Jev API, regexes, and Intl.Segmenter name-span assembly, emitting masked JSON or human reports with severity exit codes to gate sensitive text before LLM use—at the cost of sending scanned content to TypeSafe.

name: jevrealtimecodecheck
description: A VS Code/Cursor extension that checks your local git diff against Markdown-defined coding rules using TypeSafe AI's Jev model — sending only rules matching touched file types, flagging just new violations with severity scores and real line numbers — runnable on save, manually, or in CI on pull requests.

name: JevML
description: JevML is a dependency-free TypeScript toolkit of reusable ML primitives—PCA, MCMC sampling, text diffusion, and neural cellular automata—with a catalog/registry and matching/API harness that helps agents select and invoke the right primitive for a task.

name: auto-form-filler-plugin
description: A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that uses the Jev AI model to classify form fields and auto-fill locally stored profiles, handling split Japanese inputs (3-part phone, 2-part postal code, 3-select birthdates), select/radio label variations, and JSON profile import/export—while sending only field metadata (never personal values) to the API and never auto-submitting forms.

name: jev-little-airways
description: A runnable three.js air-traffic demo where every in-flight judgment—divert, hold, give way, declare emergencies, sequence landings—is made live by the Jev decision model as typed, calibrated probabilities in ~150 ms, with a monitor exposing raw API calls and costs.

name: agentOS
description: agentOS is a Linux-based agent-first operating system prototype—a complete Debian ARM64 VM with tiling terminal, Rust runtime, Python services, and gateway-backed reasoning—whose validated action broker lets an agent inspect, plan, execute, and retain knowledge under explicit user authorization.

name: jev-frontier-100
description: A 100-question four-choice benchmark comparing Jev against local Qwen3.5 models (0.8B–4B) under controlled thinking budgets, providing frozen questions, graded trial outcomes, paired bootstrap intervals, confidence diagnostics, and an offline harness to recompute all published scores.

name: jev-shell-history
description: A zsh plugin that provides fish-style autosuggestions ranked by the Jev (TypeSafe) model over your last 100 distinct history entries, showing the top match in grey after the cursor (accept with → or ^E) via non-blocking per-keystroke requests with prefix/fuzzy modes and tunable score thresholds.

name: jev-form-filler
description: A Chrome/Edge browser extension that imports your LinkedIn, X, GitHub, and portfolio pages into a reviewed local profile, then uses your own TypeSafe API key to automatically fill web forms — including embedded application forms and file uploads — with source-backed, confidence-scored answers you can inspect and undo before submitting yourself.

name: software-factory
description: A local software factory CLI that moves queued requests through YAML-defined pipelines of stages run by your installed coding-agent CLIs, shell commands, or typed judgments, each in an isolated git worktree, in parallel, with human-review gates and replayable runs.

name: jev-benchmark
description: A reproducible benchmark that evaluates TypeSafe AI's Jev on classifying agent tool calls as readonly/destructive/privileged/exfiltration using 60 labelled cases, showing 91.7% accuracy, ~400ms latency, and—most importantly—well-calibrated confidence where every error came hedged below 1.000.

name: jev-experiments
description: A compact Windows PowerShell/WPF demo that turns a folder into a semantic search surface: it sends bounded file metadata to the TypeSafe Jev API for typed decisions, fuses them with deterministic local relevance scoring to rank results, and keeps raw contents private with an offline fallback.

name: typesafe-image-diffusion
description: Generates 16x16 pixel art from text prompts by asking a multiple-choice classifier 256 parallel questions—one per pixel choosing among 16 colors—with optional local-neighborhood refinement passes, served via a FastAPI web UI and API with animated history and token usage.

name: system-one-benchmark
description: A benchmarking suite that compares TypeSafe Jev's cloud "System One" decision model against local MLX parallel constrained decoding and autoregressive Qwen baselines on adversarial and intent prompts, measuring latency, accuracy, safety precision/recall, calibration, and schema-error rates.

name: jev-llm
description: jev-llm coerces TypeSafe Jev — a judgment/classification engine — into an autoregressive language model by decoding token-by-token through multiple-choice candidate selection, offering word, char, hybrid, and syntax-aware code generation modes with temperature sampling, planning, and interactive chat.

name: typesafe-jev-workflow
description: An async LangGraph demo that classifies mocked emails via TypeSafe's Jev model into a typed `invoice`/`general` Choice and routes them to stub handlers, letting you exercise real intent-detection API calls and verify routing without sending email or payments.

name: commentlint
description: commentlint is a command-line linter that extracts comments across many languages with tree-sitter, evaluates them against configurable TypeSafe.ai yes/no rules such as active voice, and reports file/line failures for CLI, pre-commit, and CI workflows.

name: 15-min-BTC-JAP
description: A live Kalshi BTC 15-minute YES/NO trading desk that streams Coinbase BTC-USD into a TypeSafe "Jev" paper judge and fires at most one $2 order per window via `live_spin.py`, with odds/flow dashboards on ports 3000–3002 and a file-based arm/kill switch.

name: jev-voice
description: jev-voice is a macOS voice-control tool that converts speech into local app launching, typing, site searches, scrolling, shortcuts, media/system actions, and guarded multi-step browser or Accessibility-tree automation for fast hands-free desktop control.

name: jevies
description: A Python toolkit built on the TypeSafe Jev SDK whose helper "Jevs" design and review evaluation setups—recommending question types and instruction structure, checking instruction wording, option overlap, rubric ordering, and answer-space coverage, and validating inputs and test cases against preset rules.

name: typed_evals
description: A Python library and CLI that judges LLM responses, RAG datasets, and agent traces with Jev models, supporting preset and custom metrics, calibration against human labels, pluggable judge backends, and pre-execution tool guards for LangChain, CrewAI, and Microsoft Agent Framework.

name: open-jev
description: An inference harness that uses DiffusionGemma to produce typed JSON decisions by denoising a fixed token canvas and selecting the highest-logit allowed tokens, enabling training-free, schema-valid structured judgments with batched, cost-measured benchmarking.

name: site-judge
description: A CI check that audits marketing site copy for unsupported claims, combining deterministic regex checks with a probability-returning judgment model validated per-run by known-good/known-bad controls, and reports each flagged claim's sentence and score as an advisory, never-blocking PR comment.

name: jev-trade-cc
description: A point-in-time backtest of an O'Neil momentum strategy where a stateless decision model makes entry/exit calls, with reproducible pipelines, jackknife tests against mechanical rules, and timing/provenance safeguards that honestly measure whether the model adds any edge.

name: mobile-jev
description: A standalone mobile agent that drives a real Android phone through the Mobilerun API using TypeSafe's Jev model for per-step decisions—no ADB—bundling a live React streaming studio, a CLI with preview/execute modes, verified demos, JSONL execution traces, and request-level latency breakdowns for reproducible evaluation.

name: jev-emotional-avatar
description: jev-emotional-avatar renders a live Bluesky feed where the character Jev adopts avatars and outfits from user profiles and changes expressions based on post text, served locally in English or Japanese with only Node.js 22+ and a TypeSafe API key.

name: jev-assist
description: jev-assist is a CLI/agent skill that uses TypeSafe Jev to rank tracked files against a task, audit files against repo conventions, gate risky diffs, and validate ranking accuracy, making whole-repo triage cheap enough to catch relevant files grep misses.

name: jev-commit
description: A commit-msg hook that sends the staged diff and message to TypeSafe's Jev decision model, which scores five checks—filler message, diff contradiction, debug leftovers, unmentioned work, secrets—and blocks only credentials (or findings under --strict), failing open on errors.

name: jev-auto-ime
description: A macOS CLI that watches romaji keystrokes, asks TypeSafe's Jev whether the text is Japanese or English, then auto-switches the input source and retypes pending characters, skipping password fields and excluded apps with a tunable confidence threshold.

name: jev-code
description: jev-code is a coding-agent CLI and TypeScript SDK built on the decision-only Jev model: it constructs programs as syntax trees one grammar rule at a time (Python, TS/JS, C, Rust, Go, Lua, Ruby, Bash) with compiler validation, executes them with key-press approval, and exposes a scriptable `decide` command that turns stdin questions into labels, probabilities, or scores with exit-code branching.

name: OpenJev
description: OpenJev is a Windows desktop AI agent—a DeepSeek Harness fork—that consults TypeSafe's Jev decision model at every thinking step for calibrated-probability routing and verification, exposing `jev_*` tools, logging each call to a trace file, and bundling an optional Python CLI/MCP server.

name: Jev-For-Dummies
description: Jev-For-Dummies is a minimal FastAPI wrapper that exposes Jev's decision primitives—choice selection, yes/no boolean evaluation, and numeric scoring—plus a health check as plain HTTP GET endpoints returning JSON results with confidence and probabilities, requiring only a TypeSafe API key and no SDK or Jev knowledge.

name: Jevs-Garage
description: Jev's Garage is a Python 3.11+/uv workshop of 26 runnable demos and a local gallery showing how TypeSafe System One models turn realistic state into typed probabilistic judgments (Choice, Score, Noul) that deterministic policies convert into bounded actions or safe fallbacks across critical, orchestration, and casual scenarios.

name: jev-harness
description: A TypeScript library that turns TypeSafe Jev's structured `choice`/`score`/`noul` answers into production actions via a policy layer, a confidence gate for low-certainty cases, shadow mode, reusable decision recipes, and an offline eval CLI that asserts on actions rather than free text.

name: wince
description: wince is a CLI that triages any unified diff (branch, PR, or agent output) into a green/yellow/red review-attention verdict with a risk score, suggested reviewers, reasons, and experimental hunk reading order — combining non-overridable deterministic path/size rules with typed per-file model calls — so teams know where to route human review rather than having the tool review code itself.

name: peaks-notes
description: A Bun CLI and Claude Code Stop hook that incrementally maintains a topic-organized, token-budgeted markdown summary of completed conversation turns—with source provenance, an append-only archive, and an audit journal—for downstream handoffs and context compaction.

name: Jev-To-Hackathon
description: A Next.js app that matches hackathon ideas to the best-fitting NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge via Jev's structured evaluations, scoring alignment against customizable weighted criteria to reveal what already fits, what to strengthen, and the official challenge link.

name: jev-reranking
description: Benchmarks JEV's zero-shot reranking against monoBERT, BM25, and published neural systems on MS MARCO passage/document and WSJ transfer tasks, reporting nDCG@10, MAP, P@10, MRR, per-query latency, and API cost with reproducible protocols and frozen input manifests.

name: typesafe-ai-benchmark
description: A Node.js benchmark harness that runs Qwen 3.8 27B on Cerebras, TypeSafe Jev, and local Needle 3 side-by-side across seven synthetic judgment workloads, recording validated outputs, fixture agreement, latency percentiles, token usage, and API cost via a comparison theater UI with raw exportable results.

name: jev-design
description: A Next.js/shadcn logistics console and centrally governed token/family CSS engine that lets the typed Jev model turn a one-sentence brief into a coherent, catalog-constrained visual style across every component, enforced by build-time coverage gates and runtime layout audits.

name: azdaja
description: Azdaja is a recursive language-model layer that keeps full inputs in a persistent local Monty/Python evaluator, giving models a bounded surface for local computation and selective llm/llm_batch recursion—cutting tokens and steps—with optional TypeSafe typed judgments.

name: jev-vs-sovereign-benchmark
description: A benchmark suite comparing TypeSafe AI's Jev System One (`typesafe/jev-1.13` via OpenRouter) against a specialized sovereign RAG stack (DistilBERT, ColBERT-v2, DeBERTa-v3) on UK primary legislation, measuring latency, token cost, abstention, and governance reproducibility across three retrieval nodes, with dry-run and live modes producing percentile tables and SHA-256-sealed telemetry.

name: jev-ultralightspeed
description: A Python library that packs many independent text items into single TypeSafe Jev API requests to answer one judgement question per item, delivering ~32x throughput and ~41% lower cost at unchanged accuracy for batch triage, labeling, and classification queues.

name: jev-chat-jarvis
description: An Android accessibility-service chat copilot that reads on-screen WeChat/QQ/X/Feishu conversations (via UI nodes or offline OCR), uses a Jev judgment model to assess intent and risk in ~1s, and ranks three generated reply drafts it fills in but never sends—enriched by local knowledge-base, contact, and chat-history context.

name: worth-replying
description: Worth Replying is a Next.js demo that crawls a given domain, builds a customer profile, generates five X searches, and uses TypeSafe's jev model to score each tweet on five typed criteria—ICP fit, pain, reply value, needs-human, injection—routing conversations worth answering into a review queue, all via one AIsa API key.

name: similarity-ts-jev
description: A CLI and library that detects similar TypeScript functions, types, and classes with similarity-ts and fallow, then has TypeSafe's Jev model judge each pair like a code reviewer, reporting only the duplicates worth merging or refactoring.

name: building-with-jev-skill
description: An agent skill for writing and improving programs that call Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, covering question design (Choice, Score, Noul), state structure, answer composition, confidence thresholds, and diagnosing wrong or low-confidence answers, targeting `jev-1.13` and installable via Claude Code plugin, skills CLI, or manual copy.

name: jev-demo
description: A Next.js demo dashboard that triages GitHub issues into five typed Jev-1.13 decisions—category, severity, urgency, team, and actionability—with calibrated confidence thresholds, live timing/cost metrics, and Kanban or action-based views for automatic routing versus human review.

name: grok-bot-jev
description: A Python router that classifies Grok Bot requests via TypeSafe Jev's `system_one` call, returning explicit actions (reuse_cache, stop_retry, research_capped, ask_human) so shadow or active modes can skip needless browser, retry, research, or subagent work.

name: dsh-crypto-workbench
description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin providing an AI-assisted OKX USDT-perpetual trading workbench with code-enforced risk gates, an opportunity radar, human-confirmed plan execution, Jev decision monitoring, Jin10 data feeds, and a sidebar dashboard.

name: fedjev-bench
description: A pre-registered evaluation harness that ranks FOMC chair press-conference openings for inflation hawkishness via TypeSafe/Jev pairwise comparisons, validating them against same-day funds-rate changes, published FedLock scores (Gate 7 Spearman rank agreement), a TrueSkill replica, and a seven-criterion multi-axis extension, with cached results, reproducible analysis scripts, and a live re-scoring

name: laya
description: Laya is a non-autoregressive decision engine that answers typed questions (choice, score, noul) over text or JSON states in a single ~33 ms forward pass, trained with RL on strictly proper scoring rules for calibrated confidence, with a router that dispatches to one of three checkpoints across 100+ languages.

name: xo-jev
description: A Bun-based browser tic-tac-toe game where you play X against "Jev," an AI opponent that picks O moves via TypeSafe Choice (`systemOne`) through a `POST /api/move` endpoint returning move source, confidence, and probabilities, with random-cell fallback on model failure.

name: open-jev-typed-decision-engine
description: An open 150M ModernBERT encoder that answers arbitrary per-request typed questions (boolean, choice, score) about a state in one forward pass with calibrated confidences, trainable free on a Colab T4, scoring 0.697 accuracy vs TypeSafe Jev's 0.727 at ~60ms locally.

name: jgrep
description: jgrep is a Rust CLI that answers plain-English questions over piped logs, files, or directories—evaluating deduplicated context windows via the Jev SystemOne API to return yes/no probabilities, choices, or weighted scores with line-level source citations.

name: jev-review
description: A TypeSafe Jev–based code-review tool that orchestrates staged model judgments (file profiling, evidence selection, mechanism classification, severity scoring, conditional reviewer routing) over a Git diff or full codebase to flag correctness, security, reliability, compatibility, and test-coverage risks, presenting results in a localhost-only dashboard.

name: jev-gmail-ai-spam-filter-and-labeling
description: jevMail is a self-hosted Google Apps Script tool that uses the Jev AI model to label Gmail messages by meaning against custom natural-language criteria, with confidence-based second-pass review, optional auto-archiving, spend limits, and preview mode—no external backend required.

name: jev-vtuber-ime-core
description: jev-vtuber-ime-core is a TypeScript resolver/CLI that turns a Japanese reading into a canonical VTuber name by searching the web for evidence, extracting name candidates, and using Jev’s probability-only judgments to select a threshold-passing match—without bundling a dictionary or returning non-VTubers.

name: kev
description: kev is a local decision-model server — a LoRA adapter plus pointer readout head on a Qwen base (0.5B–8B) — that answers many typed questions (yes/no, multi-choice, ordinal score) about a document in one decode-free prefill pass, returning calibrated softmax probabilities through a TypeSafe System One–compatible API.

name: jot
description: Jot is a Node.js/TypeScript agent that runs the tool-calling loop for the Jev model — Jev picks tools and arguments while Jot executes calls, feeds results back into context, and iterates until a reply — shipping a chat UI with visible tool-call traces, a provider-independent core, and a loopback server that keeps credentials server-side and chats in the browser.

name: jev-traps
description: jev-traps is an Apache-2.0 TypeScript toolkit that inspects untrusted text, HTML, browser content, and images for injection risks, enforcing host-side allow/sanitize/review/block decisions through deterministic policy, optional semantic checks, and destination preflight.

name: JEV-EFMW-Syncretic-Layer
description: Reproducible synthetic testbed simulating a Jev-like typed decision layer with an EFMW-style recursive coherence monitor, providing three controlled experiments—calibration degradation, closed-loop trajectory instability, and an equal-information anti-circularity comparison—run via pip, Python scripts, and pytest under frozen null-calibrated thresholds.

name: jev-codex-plugin
description: An open-source Codex plugin that provides TypeSafe Jev decision consultation, failure diagnosis, and completion-evidence review through MCP tools, lifecycle hooks, and standalone CLI skills, returning recommendations or abstentions without acting automatically.

name: questions
description: A TypeScript library for typed semantic decisions: validate LLM answers against Zod 4 schemas or native question batches, get inferred types back via async/await or Web Streams, and swap between TypeSafe AI, Vercel AI Gateway, or generative Gemini/Claude/GPT models with retries, deadlines, and observability.

name: HA-Jev
description: A Home Assistant integration that turns typed questions for the TypeSafe Jev decision model into sensors and automation actions returning probabilities, choices, or scores, plus an Assist conversation agent, with daily token budgets and cost tracking.

name: ai-backends
description: AIBackends is a self-hostable API server that exposes ready-to-use AI endpoints for text, vision, and data tasks plus autonomous tool-using agents with multi-turn sessions and SSE streaming, backed by local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, LlamaCpp) or cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Google, Baseten, ZAI, LLM Gateway), with an admin dashboard for custom agents, HTTP tools, MCP servers,

name: open-spark-jev
description: Open Spark Jev is an open-source local decision model (spark-s1, Qwen3+LoRA) for NVIDIA DGX Spark that answers typed Choice/Score/Noul questions about a state with probabilities and confidence in ~30–66 ms, serving use cases like tool-call gating and routing.

name: tenet
description: tenet is a CLI review gate that lints agent-written diffs against plain-language rules in .tenet/config.yml, drafted from AGENTS.md-style instruction files or built-in presets, enforcing a calibrated pass/fail cutoff via git hooks so agents fix violations before review.

name: jev-design-test
description: Turns a one-line prompt into a batch of distinct, live full-page UI screens on an infinite canvas by sampling Jev's probability distributions over a fixed vocabulary of real shadcn/Base UI layout blocks — fast (~1-2s) with no generated JSX.

name: Jevbridge
description: Jevbridge is a zero-dependency Node 22 library and MCP/ACP stdio adapter that pairs any LLM with TypeSafe Jev's typed System One decisions (noul, choice, score), confidence-gating tool calls and closed-set computer-use actions so software can branch on probabilistic answers.

name: typesafe-sdk-dotnet
description: An unofficial .NET client for the TypeSafe AI API that ports the JavaScript SDK's SystemOne question primitives (Choice, Score, Noul), retry/timeout configuration, DI integration, and exception hierarchy, targeting net10.0 and netstandard2.0.

name: jev-profanity
description: A Czech-first benchmark lab that detects and star-censors unsafe review text—vulgar, rude, or coded attacks—comparing Jev (TypeSafe System One) against lexicon and token_scorer baselines, with v3.0.0 coverage of algospeak, short codes, semantic weapons, and coded hate, runnable via Node scripts with a TypeSafe API key.

name: jev-retrieval-eval
description: An evaluation harness measuring Jev as a second-stage passage filter after BM25 retrieval and as a GPT-agent retrieval tool, reporting evidence recall, latency, token usage, and per-provider API cost across controlled ranking and agent-workflow experiments on an 8-question technical corpus.

name: FeedGate
description: A Chrome extension that reduces noise across six social feeds via an explicit, reversible rule set—AI-based semantic filtering, time-limited topic mutes, author allow/mute lists, optional duplicate grouping, cosmetic filters, and honest API-usage controls—while keeping merely promotional posts visible and requiring no external server.

name: OpenRyoko
description: OpenRyoko is a Slack-first, Japanese-first resident AI gateway that gives you an AI colleague which reads the room via Haiku triage (silent/react/reply), autonomously finishes tasks using natural-language /goal stop hooks, and live-syncs all session states to a Slack Canvas.

name: laterhook
description: Laterhook is a self-hosted webhook inbox that captures every request sent to zero-setup endpoints, then lets you inspect, search, replay, tag, secure, and permanently forward matching traffic through regex routes before your real backend is ready.

name: spring-ai-typesafe
description: Spring AI TypeSafe is a Java 17+ client and Spring AI integration for TypeSafe AI’s System One API that turns a state plus typed questions into parallel structured answers for LLM judges, guardrails, RAG filtering/reranking, and tool selection without brittle generated JSON.

name: Jev-Radar
description: Jev-Radar is a local, CPU-based research workspace that turns a prompt into an auditable web investigation, combining hosted Jev decisions, Brave Search, page collection, and optional text models to produce evidence-linked comparisons, uncertainty tracking, replays, spend controls, and exports.

name: a3m-router
description: A self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible proxy that routes each prompt to the cheapest capable provider among 80+ LLMs—with semantic caching, provider fallbacks, and ensemble calls—cutting API costs by up to ~90% without changing existing client code.

name: ts-browser-agent
description: A Playwright-based browser agent that runs LangChain's `create_agent` loop with TypeSafe's classifier returning per-step probabilities over browser operations and element targets—exposing a `browse_fast` tool for deep agents and a compiled `build_browser_agent()` graph, without any third-party browser-agent package.

name: jev-robotics-demo
description: A MuJoCo simulation demo where a Franka arm with an Allegro hand stacks cubes, comparing an LLM agent that reasons step-by-step via low-level tools against Jev, a fast typed-probability model that picks pre-simulated moves — achieving the same result ~8x faster at ~1/1000th the cost.

name: pg_typesafe
description: PostgreSQL extension exposing TypeSafe AI's Noul, Choice, and Score primitives as SQL functions for yes/no probabilities, category assignment, and rubric scoring, with batched requests, retries, cancellable queries, and offline mocking.

name: n8n-nodes-jev-classification
description: An n8n community node that classifies, scores, and checks workflow items with TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model, returning typed answers with calibrated probabilities and routing items to category, yes/no, or Needs Review outputs via batched parallel requests for high-volume workflows.

name: jev-context
description: A Pi extension that replaces attention-based context management with a cheap scored judge: it routes only relevant skills, surfaces only needed tool namespaces, and prunes unhelpful tool outputs, cutting billed context ~33–37% without breaking prefix caching.

name: jev_project_context
description: An agent skill that maintains evidence-first research memory for AI coding agents, providing ten operations (init, start, frame, plan, record, end, correct, synthesize, claim-audit, doctor) with provenance gates, controlled validity vocabulary, and read-only audits so every claim stays traceable and sessions resumable.

name: doc-router
description: doc-router is a Rust CLI/library that inspects PDFs page-by-page to extract text-layer pages locally while sending only genuinely scanned pages to an OCR provider via LiteLLM, merging results into a page-ordered output that cut measured OCR cost 1.74x and latency 1.72x.

name: jev-logtriage
description: A Python triage tool that evaluates batches of Grafana/Loki logs through typed questions and confidence gates, deciding whether they warrant on-call action without executing any remediation itself.

name: jev48
description: An open, auditable reproduction of TypeSafe's Jev decision model providing a 2B checkpoint, benchmark code, frozen receipts, and audited results across six public benchmarks for verifiable independent comparison.

name: reranker
description: A reranker that scores up to 30 documents in a single call using TypeSafe's Jev model, returning a calibrated probability per document, distributed under the Apache-2.0 license.

name: typesafe-ai-php
description: A PHP 8.2+ client for the TypeSafe AI evaluation API that lets you send a state plus typed questions (yes/no "noul", multiple-choice, ordered "score") via a fluent `EvaluationRequest` and read back typed answers with probabilities, confidence, and token usage—handling retries, errors, and debug logging automatically.

name: jev-skip
description: A browser extension that detects and skips sponsor segments on unlabeled YouTube videos by sending the caption transcript to the Jev model once, painting confidence-tinted slices on the seek bar (77% recall, ~34s false skips/hour, $0.0008/video).

name: slay_the_spire_2_agent_harness
description: A macOS harness that lets AI agent CLIs (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Jev/TypeSafe) play the visible Slay the Spire 2 through a local bridge mod, with a normalized state API, tunable Markdown profiles, JSONL traces, and a dashboard tracking decisions and token costs.

name: jev-minesweeper
description: A browser-based Minesweeper demo that has TypeSafe's System One model "Jev" estimate mine probabilities via batched Noul questions, with an exact solver for confidence-gated fallback and calibration checking, plus CLI benchmarking, seeded boards, and evaluation metrics like Brier score.

name: typesafe-jev-tools
description: A Claude Code PreToolUse hook that scans JS/TS/Python writes and edits for LLM calls and hand-written classifiers, then injects a three-way test—plain code, frontier model, or a fast uncertainty-aware judgment model like Jev—so decisions that a regex could answer don't silently ship as brittle heuristics or overqualified model calls.

name: winnow
description: Winnow is a Claude Code plugin that intercepts large Read/Bash/Grep outputs, uses a calibrated probability judge to hide blocks unlikely to matter for the current task—replacing them with summarized stubs restorable via a recall key—and injects prompt-relevant memory files, cutting token costs without losing content.

name: jev-on-a-laptop
description: Reproduces parallel constrained decoding on a laptop: prefill typed schema context once, broadcast the KV cache across one batch row per field, and resolve all fields in one forward pass — schema-valid output ~7x faster than token-by-token JSON.

name: optimus-agent
description: A self-improving multi-model coding harness that pairs a native Rust application layer with a persistent Python runtime, offering recursive subagents, inspectable memory, provider-aware context compaction, background execution, and session recovery for long-running work.

name: s1decide
description: s1decide is a pre-alpha Apache-2.0 engine that answers typed questions (choice, score, true/false) about a state in one non-autoregressive forward pass over a shared prefilled cache, with masked logits forcing on-schema answers and published calibration.

name: polymarket-btc5m-jev-trading
description: A terminal agent that trades Polymarket's BTC Up/Down 5-minute markets by polling the live window each tick, asking TypeSafe Jev for a side and confidence, then buying once—via fill-or-kill orders in optional live mode, dry-run by default—or abstaining when confidence, price, edge, or time thresholds fail, holding any position to resolution.

name: hello-jev
description: A hands-on Python tutorial for building reliable systems with TypeSafe’s Jev judgment model: elicit typed noul/choice/score answers, carry context in state, route actions by confidence, and compare with ollama and Apple FM baselines.

name: fastjev
description: FastJev is an open source, self-hostable Python implementation of Jev that scores typed Choice, Boolean, and Score decisions over 2–16 options in a single logit pass across Torch, vLLM, MLX, llama.cpp, and WebGPU backends, returning probabilities, token usage, timing, and pinned model/prompt provenance for reproducible evaluation.

name: jev-311-heatmap
description: A tool that generates interactive geographic heatmaps of NYC 311 complaints through a reproducible TypeSafe JEV pipeline, letting users explore live research results and complaint patterns across the city.

name: rakitsu
description: Rakitsu is an open-source Go-based "Agent IDE" that lets you visually design multi-agent AI systems on a drag-and-drop canvas, debug them with breakpoints and time-travel execution inspection, and deploy them as a single zero-dependency binary configured via YAML with multi-provider LLM support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, LiteLLM).

name: jev-android-super
description: An Android app that completes plain-English goals on a phone by reading the accessibility UI tree, requesting ~400 ms typed actions from TypeSafe's Jev model (Gemini/OpenRouter for text), performing real taps, with STOP, purchase-block, and loop-detection safeguards.

name: glowbom-oss
description: Glowbom OSS is an open-source, local-first CLI and web app that orchestrates coding agents like OpenCode or Cursor CLI to build production-ready projects on your machine, providing stack templates, live local previews, hardened token-based security defaults, and no vendor lock-in.

name: jeview
description: Jeview is an unofficial local gateway and live visualizer for TypeSafe's Jev API that proxies requests on 127.0.0.1:4777, records every call in a local SQLite database, and renders them on a real-time map with grouping, call-linking, and display-name headers.

name: jev-market-reflex
description: A Bun/TypeScript demo that streams live Kraken BTC/ETH/SOL market data into TypeSafe AI Jev, converts compact market features into typed BUY/SELL/HOLD decisions with confidence and probabilities, and applies deterministic risk-gated paper execution with simulated P&L to a browser dashboard—no real funds or exchange credentials required.

name: noflow-runtime
description: noflow-runtime is a React 18+ package where buttons report their label and DOM context to a pluggable policy (local mock, HTTP, or server-side Jev) that selects only among app-registered affordances, with runtime safety gates for confidence thresholds, user confirmation, and error fallbacks.

name: jev-use
description: jev-use is an MCP tool and zero-dependency JS library that lets Claude Code, Codex, and pi offload text-free judgments (check/pick/rate decisions, shell-command gating, context compaction) to the Jev model via TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or Vercel backends, returning fast verdicts with confidence and escalation flags.

name: Nemotron_Jev
description: Experimental Dockerized Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-14B service that exposes a browser Decision Lab and TypeSafe-shaped API for typed choice/Noul/score questions over text or JSON, returning masked-token softmax distributions, selections, weighted scores, and confidence for local probability inspection.

name: sarvam-jev
description: sarvam-jev answers multiple-choice decisions on Sarvam's Indic models by softmaxing logits over lettered answer slots rather than generating text, amortizing one prefilled KV state across many questions for fast, cheap decisions that cannot be malformed.

name: jev-t-rex-runner
description: A standalone ES6 port of Chromium's T-Rex Runner game—stripped of browser dependencies and circular imports, exposing a `Runner` class with speed, input, sound, and state controls—optionally playable by TypeSafe's Jev AI model, which picks `jump`, `duck`, or `keep_running` maneuvers via a local Node server that keeps the API key server-side.

name: ruby_llm
description: RubyLLM is a Ruby-native AI framework providing one consistent API across 18 providers for chat, agents, tools, structured output, streaming, embeddings, reranking, image/video/audio generation, transcription, OCR, and moderation, with Rails integration and cost tracking.

name: rh-guard
description: rh-guard is a hook-layer gate for coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Grok Build, Pi, Amp, Prime Agent, DeepSeek Harness, plus Exo via ToolRuntime wrap) that intercepts tool calls to block reward hacking—tampering with graders, hidden tests, or the eval process—while steering agents toward checks they cannot game.

name: jevfanity
description: Jevfanity is a Cloudflare Workers moderation API that evaluates text in parallel across profanity, slur, harassment, threat, and sexual categories via Jev's Noul primitive, returning per-category probabilities under configurable levels and thresholds, plus a typed npm SDK.

name: fast-jev-compaction
description: A Claude Code plugin that replaces standard compaction summaries with Jev decision-making, scoring every tool call and result in a single fast request so stale items are dropped or truncated while retained content stays verbatim.

name: bezel
description: Bezel is a Nix flake overlay that supplements an existing agent harness (omp, cursor-agent, Grok Build) with a skills tree and Jev, a shadow-first policy gate whose router, adapters, and diff check issue continue/stop/escalate verdicts via Typesafe.

name: jevonian
description: Jevonian is a local proxy that sits between your coding agent and LLM providers, routing each turn to the most cost-effective capable model, managing quota and cache economics across API-key and subscription accounts, and logging every routing decision to a local ledger.

name: typesafe-local
description: A local server that answers typed questions (yes/no, choice, score) about a document by encoding it once into a reusable KV cache and softmaxing a single position's logits over legal answer tokens, returning calibrated probability distributions instead of generated text.

name: jev-paint
description: jev-paint is a local browser app that turns Jev pixel probability distributions into 560×560 impasto-style paintings—sampling spatially correlated pigments, luminance-contour strokes, and entropy-driven relief in a web worker—while a loopback Python helper forwards API requests without storing keys.

name: typesafe-router-pipeline
description: An Open WebUI Pipelines function that classifies each chat message by cost tier and code-vs-text kind, then routes it through ordered OpenRouter/OrcaRouter model lists with failover—so simple prompts hit cheap models while complex ones reach stronger backends.

name: quorum
description: quorum re-implements TypeSafe's SystemOne contract locally and privately—typed noul/choice/score questions answered with probabilities read from constrained-decode logprobs on any llama-server endpoint—plus a logging, labeling, and temperature-calibration loop that turns logged judgments into a fine-tuning corpus.

name: typesafe-sdk-go
description: Go client for the TypeSafe AI API that sends batched typed questions (yes/no, choice, score) about a piece of state to System One models and returns calibrated probabilities with confidence scores, retries, timeouts, and a fake-server test package requiring no API key.

name: pi-jev-skill-picker
description: A Pi extension that strips the ~19k-token skills catalog from model requests and adds `skill_search`/`skill_load` tools that use TypeSafe's Jev model to rank enabled skills per task and load only relevant SKILL.md files on demand, cutting prompt cost ~87% (with lexical fallback).

name: omp-jev-compaction
description: An omp plugin that verbatim-reduces context by scoring every tool call and result with TypeSafe's Jev decision model (via TypeSafe API or OpenRouter), truncating stale outputs to recoverable spill-file notes while preserving all text and call records, with sticky decisions that rarely break the provider's prompt cache.

name: pi-typesafe
description: A Pi extension that judges bash, write, and edit calls with four pre-flight hazard checks and four post-edit rubric checks via TypeSafe Jev, in advisory, shadow, or blocking modes with configurable thresholds and fail-open assessment recording plus feedback injection.

name: classifier-dev
description: A free, keyless Cloudflare Worker API and npm CLI that assigns caller-supplied labels to plain text—up to 1,000 items per request—returning calibrated confidence scores, with per-IP rate limiting, LLM fallback chains, agent feedback endpoints, and per-request cost analytics.

name: typesafe-ai
description: typesafe-ai is a Rust client for TypeSafe's System One evaluation API, returning typed Noul, Choice, and Score judgments with probabilities, confidence, and usage data over sync or async HTTP clients, with batched questions, observable retries, and inspectable errors.

name: jev_local
description: A local API server that returns choice/score/noul probabilities for questions over text, JSON, and images in TypeSafe's `/v1/systemone` format, using either zero-shot LFM2.5 logprobs via llama.cpp or a fine-tuned ModernBERT-Ja cross-encoder backend.

name: typesafeai-dotnet-sdk
description: A community-maintained .NET SDK for TypeSafe AI's System One API that answers typed yes/no, choice, and rubric-score questions about text or JSON state in one parallel request, returning probability-backed answers with retries, DI, and forward-compatible raw-JSON handling.

name: gen-ui
description: A benchmarking UI picker that times TypeSafe AI’s Jev model as it turns arbitrary JSON into shadcn/ui displays—via page templates, per-field composition, and live API feeds—while reporting Jev, round-trip, p50, and p95 latency.

name: project_blackout
description: BLACKOUT is a local interactive cybersecurity lab that generates synthetic company telemetry, runs configurable attack and benign scenarios, records and replays Jev risk judgments, and exposes evidence, policies, timing, and investigation state so operators can inspect what the model detects, misses, and why.

name: dlq_inspector
description: Local-first CLI for inspecting RabbitMQ and Redis Streams dead-letter queues: it groups failures by cause, then recovers messages only through dry-run plans, explicit --confirm, and rate limits—snapshotting replays for rollback and logging every action to a local audit trail.

name: decider
description: decider is a fine-tuned language model that reads a state plus typed questions (choice, score, yes/no) and returns calibrated probabilities over the answer options in one forward pass—no decoding—served via a cached, TypeSafe-compatible HTTP API for fast structured decisions.

name: system-one-open
description: An MIT-licensed open replica of TypeSafe's Jev decision model — Gemma 4 E2B (LoRA) and Gemma 3 270M trained and served on Modal — that turns state into typed calibrated `choice`/`score`/`noul` decisions in one forward pass, with full data, training, eval, and demo code.

name: jev-plays-games
description: A Node.js web app that lets you play chess or Connect Four against the Jev language model (or watch it play itself) via OpenRouter, describing board state and legal moves as a multiple-choice question and displaying the model's move probabilities, confidence, and per-turn cost.

name: hermes-jev-context-engine
description: An experimental Hermes Agent context-engine plugin that asks TypeSafe Jev at compaction time which eligible older web_search tool results are obsolete, archiving the transcript and replacing pruned bodies with markers when checks pass—or falling back to native compression when unsafe—with an installer, offline tests, a read-only `/jev-status` skill, and evaluation docs for measuring whether pr

name: is-malicious
description: A Node.js CLI that sends a project's source, config, build, and CI files to the TypeSafe Jev API to flag hidden, deceptive, or data-stealing behavior, reporting suspicious file/line locations with severity, token cost, and CI-ready exit codes for local or PR-diff scans.

name: jev-graalvm
description: GraalVM-native Java service that fetches live Open-Meteo forecasts, asks TypeSafe's JEV model for typed choice/fit/comfort decisions (with a transparent local demo mode when no API key is set), and renders the verdict on a localhost:8080 web UI.

name: openvons
description: openvons makes frozen LLM, vision, and speech models answer finite option sets with calibrated probabilities—including a "none of the above"—split into execute/confirm/reject decisions, and its JevPick menu-picking gives 3–5x faster tool-call decoding.

name: AssertLens
description: AssertLens is a dependency-free Node 24.12+ CLI that runs sandboxed executable checks (via Bubblewrap on Linux) against Git working trees or commits and sends selected files' before/after contents with named falsifiable assertions to the Jev model for advisory supported/contradicted/insufficient verdicts in local and GitHub PR workflows.

name: jev-claim-vs-measured
