description: A reproducible test suite measuring TypeSafe's Jev model on Binance perpetuals — latency, calibration, and returns at 1-second and 15–60-minute horizons — showing no tradeable edge versus a one-line rule, with all model responses cached for verification without an API key.

name: jevspeak
description: JevSpeak is a chat system where a decision model (Jev) answers ~13 parallel questions about each user message to produce a typed semantic IR that a deterministic compiler renders into English (or other locale packs) with confidence-calibrated hedging—demonstrating natural conversation without any generative LLM in the runtime pipeline.

name: JevPlaysPokemon
description: A demo harness that lets the Jev model play real Pokémon FireRed fights on mGBA (reading battle state from RAM) and Pokémon Showdown matches by feeding it per-turn JSON snapshots of HP, stats, and legal moves/switches, executing its typed choices, and exposing a live dashboard with replays.

name: typesafe-sdk-go
description: An unofficial Go SDK for the TypeSafe AI API that provides a configurable client, typed SystemOne questions and choice/score/noul answers, model listing, structured API errors, and runnable live-API examples.

name: jev-nethack
description: Public source, live gameplay viewer, archived recordings, and research artifacts for Jev, an AI agent persistently playing NetHack — including the runner, crash-recovery background service, BC/PPO training pilots, sanitized transition datasets, and rigorously documented negative-result experiments.

name: jev-trade
description: A Bun trading bot that reads the Hyperliquid book every tick, lets the Jev model call long/short and open/close/hold across five isolated coin wallets, sends post-only maker entries and Ioc exits, and streams fills and positions to a live Next dashboard, with dry-run and testnet modes.

name: code-compact-jev
description: An npm library, CLI, and Claude Code plugin that uses a calibrated classifier to score comments in JS/TS/Rust/Go/Python as drop, shorten, extend, or keep, then applies LLM rewrites only to survivors while guaranteeing code is never modified.

name: five-lines
description: five-lines is a cross-platform CLI that reviews pull-request diffs against the ten *Five Lines of Code* refactoring rules, combining deterministic tree-sitter checks in ten languages with optional probabilistic Jev judgments, suppression controls, JSON output, thresholds, and CI failure gates.

name: mario-never-dies
description: A demo that uses microsandbox VM snapshots to checkpoint a running Mario game every 150 frames and, on each death, branches the last checkpoint into four VM copies racing different recoveries so the survivor becomes the run, while the Jev API picks moves from parsed RAM state and a browser visualizes the branching timelines.

name: safer-with-jev
description: Safer with Jev is a live demo site and API exposing TypeSafe Jev endpoints that inspect request bodies for prompt injections or unsafe replies and optionally forward the same bytes to a caller-chosen HTTPS target only when the judgment passes.

name: watfile
description: watfile is a Python CLI that sorts files (incl. PDFs) into category folders via symlink, copy, or move by sending each document's text extract to a typed decision model—batched TypeSafe Jev API calls or a local offline Laya backend—with confidence gating and a dry-run mode.

name: MinusPodJev
description: MinusPodJev is a FastAPI proxy exposing TypeSafe Jev to MinusPod as an OpenAI-compatible ad-detection model, scoring transcript segments into classified, sponsor-matched spans with runtime thresholds and a status UI, plus an offline benchmark comparing Jev to 84 chat models.

name: jev-mcp
description: MCP server exposing ten fast, low-cost judgment tools (verify, screen, find, rerank, classify, decide, compare, extract, review, gate) that return typed probabilities and confidence scores so agents can fact-check claims, detect prompt injection, rank candidates, and validate diffs without a frontier model.

name: jev-code
description: jev-code is a TypeScript SDK and CLI that lets the decision-only Jev model pick among finite alternatives to build validated AST programs in many languages, run coding sessions, and power a `decide` command whose exit codes let scripts branch on labels, probabilities, or scores.

name: jev-prune-kit
description: jev-prune-kit provides a capability-aware context-pruning installer, a bounded Jev assessment engine, and experimental request-projection adapters for harness integration, enabling controlled context reduction and evaluation workflows that remain experimental and untested on live hosts.

name: twitter-timeline-analyzer
description: A Chrome extension that filters your Twitter/X timeline by natural-language topics—an LLM generates regex patterns and decision rules, TypeSafe's Jev or any OpenAI-compatible API scores each tweet in real time, and matches get tagged, highlighted, or hidden with feedback-driven refinement.

name: jevons
description: Jevons is a local, embeddable System One server exposing `POST /v1/systemone` per the TypeSafe HTTP contract, scoring allowed outcomes from LFM2.5 logits and assembling the response JSON in code, with failover routing to an optional Laya encoder or official TypeSafe cloud.

name: jev-terminal-browser-driver
description: A CLI driver that runs an autonomous observe→choose→act loop on terminal-browser (terminal-rendered Chromium), using Jev typed-decision calls via OpenRouter instead of screenshots or DOM dumps—~$0.0001/decision, ~200-byte JSON ticks, code-enforced tab-lease safety.

name: ailang-packages
description: A monorepo of tested, reusable AILANG packages extracted from production projects, providing modules for GCP auth, HTTP helpers, logging, config, Firestore, billing/Stripe, contract reasoning, and typed decisions, installable via registry, path, or git-subdir dependencies.

name: ask-jev
description: A zero-dependency Python CLI for bounded advisory judgments—choice, evidence checks, ordinal scoring, batches, verbatim passage extraction—via TypeSafe's System One model, returning confidence-gated answers, escalation signals, and evidence receipts inside a 280ms budget.

name: feedwall
description: Feedwall is a dependency-free Manifest V3 browser extension for Chrome-based browsers that filters feeds on X, YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, and Hacker News by sending each post to a fast yes/no-probability model (TypeSafe's Jev) under your own API key, letting you define custom plain-English topics with Keep/Hide/Dim/Highlight actions, per-site focus mode, a test-on-recent-posts preview, mistake fee

name: jevmail
description: Jevmail is an open-source, read-only Gmail triage app that sorts messages into five trays with 1–5 urgency scores using TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model via Vercel AI Gateway—about a minute and 3 cents per 1,000 emails—with all state in local SQLite.

name: pi-jev-wiki
description: pi-jev-wiki is an agent-managed wiki that maintains a project's conceptual space, using Jev to keep its accumulated knowledge legitimate, relevant, and robust as it scales.

name: open-typesafe-camoufox
description: A CLI that drives a headed Camoufox browser toward plain-English tasks at ~$0.0002/step via deterministic page reads, a confidence-gated Jev classifier over typesafe_sdk, a writer model only for free text, and a ranked CAPTCHA-solver chain with full audit trails.

name: ground-truth
description: A browser extension that automatically rates the political lean of the article in your current tab — painting an L/C/R/MIX toolbar badge and a side panel with bias shares, piece type, topic, and language loadedness — via a source-blind TypeSafe call proxied through a reading service, so no API key or host permissions ship in the build.

name: jev-dns-filter
description: A dependency-free Go sidecar that pairs with Knot Resolver to filter DNS: it scores each queried domain via TypeSafe's jev AI model, returns NODATA for domains exceeding per-category thresholds, forwards the rest upstream, and fails open on errors.

name: typesafe-ai-playground
description: `typesafe-ai` is a Rust CLI playground for TypeSafe's Jev model that scores text files for HIPAA-style PHI metrics, rates code comments on accuracy and usefulness, ranks per-line runtime importance into a JSONL heat map viewable in a local browser, and provides live interactive tone analysis.

name: jev-browser
description: Headless browser agent (MCP, CLI, or library) in which TypeSafe's Jev model chooses one action per step from a page's interactive elements and scores goal/stuck probability, returning the final page, step trace, console errors, and screenshot at sub-cent cost.

name: compact-adviser
description: compact-adviser is a plugin for Pi, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Grok that scores each settled turn via TypeSafe's Jev model against a context-fill-adjusted threshold to hint—or, where supported and opted in, automatically run—/compact when the session reaches a safe boundary.

name: readybase-public
description: ReadyBase is a local-first CLI that maps repo dependencies, blast radius, ownership, and conventions to score AI-readiness, flag drift in AI-written code, guard risky edits, and certify the autonomy level (L0–L3) a codebase can safely support.

name: Jev-StepPilot
description: A Windows-only Tauri desktop agent that autonomously carries out a typed goal by watching the active window and asking Jev for each next step—launching apps via Start-menu search, pausing on uncertain or hard-to-undo actions, and aborting when the mouse hits a screen corner.

name: jev-flight-combat
description: A 3D browser flight-combat game with manual keyboard controls, a deterministic local AI pilot, and live Jev model decisions via Vercel AI Gateway through a loopback Node server, featuring Three.js rendering, HUD/radar, telemetry export, and headless verification runs.

name: hermes-jev-approvals
description: A Hermes Agent plugin that routes smart command-approval decisions through TypeSafe's Jev model, replacing a chat LLM's one-token verdict with six parallel calibrated questions plus code-level policy rules for secret exfiltration, self-advocacy, blast radius, and operator allowlists—cutting approval latency ~10x while logging every decision.

name: jpp
description: J++ is an experimental programming language—implemented as a Rust-native CLI with a retained Python reference—that treats questions and methods as composable values, letting programs construct adaptive queries, accept and return methods, and execute semantic-judgment-driven algorithms offline.

name: jevymarket
description: A Polymarket trading bot that pairs TypeSafe's Jev calibrated-probability model with a web-searching researcher to price news-driven markets, placing Kelly-sized GTC limit orders where Jev's edge beats the order book, under hard exposure caps with SQLite logging.

name: jev-axi
description: jev-axi is a CLI for TypeSafe's Jev model, which answers typed questions with calibrated probabilities in ~400ms, giving agents a cheap second opinion: hooks that block risky commands, injection screening of fetched text, log triage, diff review, and file ranking.

name: armin
description: ARMIN is a per-project sidecar that passively captures agent sessions, distills durable decisions, rules, and open items into a queryable graph, and injects a compact reasoning-state brief each turn and after compaction so prior reasoning survives and prevents re-decision drift.

name: jev-telop-live
description: A macOS tool that turns live camera-and-microphone speech into automatic Japanese variety-show captions, sound-effect words, manga visual effects, and mood-driven sunglasses/voice changes, by sending transcripts to the Jev API with 30 typed questions and firing effects under code-controlled timing rules.

name: hermes-jev-router
description: An experimental opt-in Hermes plugin that previews and returns policy-constrained model routing plans—provider/model IDs plus an output cap—using TypeSafe Jev complexity assessment, explicit approval hashing, capability/cost/token/latency checks, and a configured fallback without dispatching requests.

name: jev-hanko
description: Benchmark toolkit comparing TypeSafe AI's Jev model against fast, cheap LLMs on a 41-clause contract-page classification task over 500 CUAD pages, providing reproduction scripts, per-page latency/cost/recall/precision/F1 measurements, and replayable browser demos of the recorded runs.

name: filelathe
description: Filelathe is a web app that turns a dropped file or pasted URL into a floating window with the right tool—media player, editor, inspector, or an AI-invented mini-app for unknown formats—combining Jev's typed routing and composition with Haiku-generated UI Specs.

name: jev-extraction-marker-recovery
description: A Python script that recovers footnote and citation markers lost when OCR flattens superscripts, using a recall-heavy tokenizer to surface suspicious tokens and Jev (TypeSafe) to classify each as citation, footnote, section label, unit/exponent, or non-marker for reinsertion.

name: fast-jev-opencode
description: An OpenCode v2 plugin that prunes stale tool calls and bulky results from outgoing model requests via TypeSafe's Jev through the `context` hook—leaving stored history untouched, failing open on errors, caching decisions across requests, and defaulting to observe-only dry-run mode.

name: jevals
description: jevals is a Python eval and guardrail library that checks agent traces — tool choice, groundedness, scope, relevancy, injection, PII — by packing all typed questions into one cheap, fast Jev-style decision-model request instead of an expensive nondeterministic LLM judge.

name: hermes-jev-skills
description: Eight agent-agnostic skills and a Hermes plugin that delegate per-turn decisions—model routing, memory filtering, compaction, skill selection, triage, GUI/browser actions—to TypeSafe's Jev decision model (~0.4 s, ~$0.00006), with redacted payloads and fail-open fallbacks.

name: jev-guard
description: jev-guard is a security hook that uses the Jev API to risk-score every tool call before execution, flag prompt injection in tool results, and audit skill/instruction files for covert behavior, working across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, Cursor, pi, OpenCode, and ACP.

name: Jev-Trades
description: Jev-Trades pairs a Next.js dashboard with a Python yfinance feed to stream one-minute crypto candles, compute indicators, request TypeSafe trading decisions, and apply them to a risk-limited simulated multi-asset portfolio for broker-free strategy testing.

name: pi-warden
description: pi-warden supervises Pi coding sessions by checking commands, edits, replies, and subagent reports for risky actions, rule violations, stuck loops, unverified “done” claims, secrets, runaway output, and noise, steering the agent to self-correct or holding irreversible steps.

name: zammad-jev-dispatcher
description: A Zammad integration that uses Jev (TypeSafe AI) to automatically triage incoming tickets, classifying each one and routing it to the appropriate service group so support teams can skip manual sorting and reach the right queue faster.

name: jev-curate
description: jev-curate is a Rust/Python CLI and library that streams Parquet/JSONL datasets through TypeSafe AI's Jev model to filter and score synthetic or pretraining rows at high throughput using typed decisions, calibrated probabilities, rubric presets, and adaptive rate limiting.

name: jevbrain
description: Jev Brain is a sub-millisecond local pre-execution firewall for AI agents and LLM apps that intercepts tool calls, shell commands, and commits to block destructive actions, secret leaks, and runaway loops via SDK wrappers, a GitHub Action, git hooks, CLI, and REST API.

name: jevchat
description: jevchat is a tool that turns Jev into a chatbot, providing a conversational interface layer so users can interact with Jev through chat-style prompts and responses rather than its default interface.

name: lgtm
description: lgtm is a CLI that audits test files or diffs against their implementations with a bring-your-own-model reviewer to flag vacuous, mock-bound, or otherwise non-proving tests, estimate cost/runtime before running, and fit into terminal, CI, or agent workflows.

name: pr-sieve
description: pr-sieve is a GitHub Action that treats a base-ref `.jev.yml` of typed TypeSafe Jev questions as a semantic PR linter, failing, commenting, or passing check runs on scored answers plus code-level secret detection—never writing reviews or approving changes.

name: jevframe
description: jevframe adds a `.jev` accessor to pandas and Polars DataFrames for per-row AI text classification, sentiment analysis, and rubric scoring via natural-language questions, returning labels, confidences, and full probability distributions with bounded concurrency, caching, and null/error policies.

name: laya-jev-api
description: A FastAPI/uvicorn server for Apple Silicon that exposes the jev-compatible `POST /v1/systemone` endpoint—answering noul (yes/no), choice, and score questions against shared JSON state via local Laya Core ML inference—with optional bearer auth, health probes, request-ID tracing, and env/CLI configuration.

name: jevsubrouter
description: JevSubRouter is a dependency-free Claude Code plugin whose hooks route each sub-agent dispatch to the cheapest sufficient model tier—without touching the orchestrator's cached prefix—with fail-open routing, worker background context, and /jev-why/jev-stats observability.

name: typesafe-go
description: Community-maintained, stdlib-only Go client for the TypeSafe AI API that returns typed structured answers (Noul probabilities, Choices, Scores) via `SystemOne`, with `errors.As`-compatible typed errors, configurable retries/backoff, context-aware concurrency safety, and per-call overrides for model, timeout, and headers.

name: jev-lm
description: jev-lm turns TypeSafe’s Jev option classifier into a character-level autoregressive language model that generates short answers over `a-z`, space, and a stop option, with calibrated probabilities, order averaging, greedy or beam decoding, CLI sessions, and a Python API.

name: jev-codex-token-saver
description: Jev Codex Token Saver is a Codex plugin whose local MCP server scans workspaces or large logs, sends bounded candidate excerpts to Jev for typed relevance scoring, and returns only selected excerpts—reducing tokens sent to Codex, with deterministic local fallback when its API key is unavailable.

name: ask-jev-skill
description: A Hermes skill that invokes TypeSafe Jev (`jev-latest`) as a typed decision tiebreaker, returning probabilistic Choice, Score, or Noul answers so agents can act confidently or escalate, with install, env-key, disable, and reliability-test scripts.

name: jev-acento
description: jev-acento is a reproducible audit quantifying how TypeSafe AI's Jev evaluation model loses accuracy, calibration, and automatable coverage on Spanish inputs, plus a CLI (`acento`) for running the same paired-language comparison on your own labelled data.

name: jev-trader
description: A Monad trading bot that queries a TypeSafe Jev model each ~300 ms block for a buy/sell call on Kuru's MON-USDC book and posts a post-only limit order one tick inside the touch—earning spread on taker fills—with dry-run mode, sub-block two-RPC-round-trip hot loop, and an SSE dashboard server streaming per-block quotes, fills, and P&L.

name: typesafeai-go
description: A Go client library for the TypeSafe AI API that sends typed questions—Noul (yes/no probability), Choice (options), and Score (ordered levels)—via a SystemOne client and returns answers in corresponding Go types, enabling type-safe model querying.

name: invalidate
description: invalidate is a Python library that continuously checks every stored agent memory against each new event—using the ~150 ms, $0.00006-per-check Jev yes/no model plus fixed rules—to mark stale facts superseded or contradicted without editing them, route uncertain cases to human review, and layer onto existing stores like Mem0, Chroma, or pgvector so agents stop answering from outdated memories.

name: jevgate
description: JevGate is a CLI that reviews selected source files with TypeSafe Jev for organization, simplification, and shared-logic concerns, offering reports, JSON output, context controls, role assessment, caching, and upload limits for iterative or CI checks.

name: piper-astra-jev
description: piper-astra-jev provides eight Jupyter-notebook demo runs that drive a real AgileX PiPER arm with large models, comparing Astra and Jev deciders across Grounding DINO, SAM 3, and STL-geometry perception for grasping, balanced carrying, and ~2 mm-clearance insertion.

name: KaLM-Jev
description: KaLM-Jev is a local PyTorch/Transformers service that wraps the KaLM-Reranker-V1-R2 reranker to return structured Choice/Score/Noul judgments (probabilities, expected scores, yes/no margins) via HTTP or Python, with an LRU document cache and no text generation.

name: jev-semgrep
description: jev-semgrep is a cross-language semantic grep that scores every line against a meaning you specify, letting you search English text in Japanese or vice versa and combine meanings with AND/OR/NOT logic for precise concept-based search.

name: jev-compare
description: jev-compare is a comparison utility that lets users evaluate differences between inputs, useful for quickly spotting discrepancies during development or review workflows.

name: jev-align
description: jev-align is an experimental CLI that iteratively improves TypeSafe Jev AI Functions by surfacing uncertain dataset rows for human labeling, running GEPA optimization with configurable reflection models and providers (TypeSafe, Vercel, Cloudflare), and resumable runs that can keep learning from captured production examples.

name: tabjev
description: A Chrome extension that automatically sorts every newly opened tab into the right tab group by asking the Jev API a typed choice question with a calibrated probability, at roughly a cent per thousand tabs.

name: kev
description: Kev is a local System One decision engine that turns unstructured state into typed probabilistic answers (Noul/Choice/Score) by scoring option-token logits instead of generating text, so invalid labels are impossible and applications get thresholdable distributions via Python, HTTP, or CLI.

name: jev-downloads-sorter
description: A macOS launchd agent that watches ~/Downloads and uses Jev decisions, with an offline extension-map fallback, to route each finished file or folder into your configured folders without overwrites using filename, type, size, source URL, and content hints.

name: jev-crash-course
description: An 11-level (~65 min) hands-on crash course on Jev, TypeSafe AI's fast "System One" decision model, with runnable real-API Python examples, a tested capstone project, and LiteLLM support for any provider—teaching cheap calibrated gating around LLM generation in agent loops.

name: second-thought
description: Second Thought is a terminal hook that AI-judges each shell command before it runs—allowing, warning, or blocking it—with a calibrated multiple-choice judge, pre-judging secret redaction, fail-open behavior, a typed `YES` override, a local audit log, and a free keyless mock mode for demos.

name: simple-jev
description: Simple Jev is a local Hugging Face/PyTorch server that turns shared context plus choice, rubric-score, or truth questions into JSON answers by scoring next-token logits, reusing the common prompt’s KV cache to avoid generated completions and repeated prefill.

name: QuantDinger
description: QuantDinger is an open-source, self-hosted AI trading platform that turns trading ideas into Python strategies with multi-provider AI research, server-side backtesting, paper and live execution across crypto exchanges and brokers, plus monitoring via web, mobile, API, and MCP interfaces backed by PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery workers.

name: jev-document-classification
description: Local-first app that sorts documents into configured folders via typesafe-ai/jev on Vercel AI Gateway, quarantining unreadable, low-confidence, or injection-suspect files, with bounded 4,500-char local profiles, batched requests, preview, undo, and cost audits.

name: abide
description: Abide is a CLI that hooks Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode to check every edit or turn against repository instruction rules via TypeSafe’s Jev decision model, catching violations linters miss, prompting in-turn repairs, and providing audit, calibration, cost, and reporting commands.

name: jev-migrate
description: A CLI tool that scans TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python code for LLM calls that are just routing, scoring, or yes/no decisions, then reports confidence-scored detections, estimated cost/latency savings, and scaffolds for converting them to local TypeSafe Jev rules.

name: laya-server
description: A local FastAPI server that runs the Laya decision model behind TypeSafe's Jev/System One wire API — a drop-in, keyless replacement returning calibrated probabilities for typed noul/choice/score questions in one forward pass, with three selectable checkpoints, a built-in /demo UI, and a CLI.

name: jev-legal-instrumentation-latam
description: A reproducible Spanish-language pilot benchmarking typed-decision classification on 30 public Argentine Supreme Court metadata records—comparing deterministic rules, a local 0.5B model, and the Jev SDK—to show that high model confidence does not equal legal correctness.

name: typesafe-cookie-consent
description: Chrome extension that replaces filter lists with TypeSafe's Jev decision model to read cookie banners and popups, pick and click the decline button (drilling into settings layers when needed), while hard-ignoring user-action dialogs; bring-your-own-key, no backend.

name: jevshield
description: jevshield is a Python middleware library that gates AI agent tool calls through single-pass, non-autoregressive security evaluations using TypeSafe's Jev models — combining risk-tier, destructiveness-probability, and blast-radius primitives to block dangerous actions in under 100ms, with decorator and LangChain integrations plus a zero-config local heuristic fallback.

name: jev-mcp
description: jev-mcp is a local stdio MCP server that gives hosts like Cursor and Codex nine typed TypeSafe Jev judgment tools — for routing steps, selecting prepared tool calls, reviewing patches, verifying claims, screening content, ranking candidates, and gating — returning Choice/Score/Noul answers with confidence and auto/review/escalate actions while the host executes tools itself.

name: typesafe-cli
description: typesafe-cli is a `jev` shell command that pipes state plus typed questions (noul probabilities, multi-option choices, rubric scores) to the Jev API and returns typed answers, batching many questions into one ~0.3s request with key resolution, retries, and JSON output.

name: dag-jev
description: A Rust tool (`cargo run`) that reads test input from `input.txt`, renders dependency graphs via `render.sh` into `core/out`, and lets you verify its Jev output against control dependencies generated by `generate_control.py` using a `dep_{}_{}: 0/1` format.

name: toxic-filter
description: A Chrome extension (MV3, Chrome 120+) that sends X post text to the TypeSafe Jev API using your own API token, classifies it into six toxicity categories (discrimination, trolling, hate, calls to attack, sneering, resignation), and hides posts above a configurable probability threshold (default 70%) behind a dismissible translucent overlay.

name: pi-jev
description: A Pi extension that pairs local coding models with hosted TypeSafe Jev judgments to cut end-to-end latency via ranked file-excerpt retrieval, large-tool-output focusing, optional skill hints and Qwen thinking control, plus caching and outage cooldowns.

name: jev-system-architect
description: A system-architecture skill that guides agents in decomposing TypeSafe Jev integrations—deciding where fuzzy semantic judgment should become bounded Choice, Score, or Noul questions while deterministic code keeps control flow, side effects, batching, and explicit uncertainty routing.

name: typesafe-adblock
description: A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that heuristically collects ad-shaped DOM candidates on any page, sends compact JSON descriptions in batched requests to TypeSafe AI's Jev model (BYOK, no backend), and removes or highlights elements whose ad probability exceeds a configurable threshold.

name: jev-test-filter
description: CLI tool that scores every test in a repository against a git diff via TypeSafe's Jev model in one round trip, then emits or directly executes the correct selection arguments for vitest, jest, node --test, Playwright, cargo test, or go test so only plausibly affected tests run.

name: JevVSPolymarket
description: JevVSPolymarket is a Node.js/pnpm toolkit that benchmarks the Jev model's probability forecasts on settled Polymarket sports/esports markets—scoring Brier and accuracy against historical market-price baselines via batch, repeat, and background-ablation experiments without trading.

name: TypeLLM
description: TypeLLM is a client for type-safe constrained decoding on SGLang-served open LLMs, producing JSON Schema–typed outputs (enums, booleans, integers, numbers, text) with no out-of-schema values, prefix caching, sequential or batch execution, optional thinking, and sampling.

name: typesafe-chess
description: Local app that tests TypeSafe Jev as a chess decision-maker: chess.js lists the legal moves, Jev picks one, and Stockfish grades it, with configurable prompt setups, an adaptive Stockfish ladder, mock mode, a stats dashboard, and headless benchmarks.

name: arc-cua
description: arc-cua is a macOS action layer that lets any planner or LLM hand off bounded desktop subtasks (goal, inputs, verification, constraints) to a fast decision backend called JEV, which executes the observe–act UI loop over structured AX + OCR elements—eliminating expensive frontier-model reasoning for every click.

name: callee
description: Callee defines repeatable agent workflows as versioned YAML/Markdown resources that compose AI roles, shell scripts, human approvals, and typed model decisions via sequential, parallel, loop, and router control flow, validated pre-run and invocable from terminal or coding agents.

name: typesafe-jev-bridge
description: A zero-dependency Node.js bridge that exposes TypeSafe's Jev model—which answers typed yes/no, choice, and rubric-score questions with calibrated probabilities—as OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus a CLI, code-audit tool, and autofix loop usable from any OpenAI client.

name: Jev-Quantum
description: A Rust stochastic baseline server implementing the Jev System One protocol (`noul`/`choice`/`score`) that answers requests with sub-microsecond PRNG output instead of reading prompts, serving as a dummy/mock and lower bound for latency and agent-routing benchmarks.

name: OneVOneJev
description: OneVOneJev is a server-authoritative browser FPS where players queue to quickscope-duel an AI opponent ("Jev") in a 60 Hz WebSocket arena — first to 5 kills — with spectating, chat, killcam replays, and a TypeSafe-powered/heuristic AI.

name: jev4k
description: jev4k is a Kotlin DSL and client library for TypeSafe's Jev model that lets you declare typed yes/no, multiple-choice, and ordinal-score questions about a given state, send them in one request, and receive calibrated typed answers—including enum-valued options—with probabilities and confidence your code can branch on.

name: JevUnreal
description: JevUnreal is an Unreal Engine 5.8 plugin that adds async Blueprint nodes (Yes/No, Choose, Probability, plus a raw request node) which send game-state descriptions to the TypeSafe Jev API and return AI decisions with confidence and latency, supporting direct API-key or proxied requests for packaged builds.

name: Jev-Mem
description: Jev-Mem is an agentic memory system for long-running AI agents: a lightweight System-One controller manages memory writing and retrieval over semantic, temporal, causal, and entity graph views, while a System-Two model synthesizes answers, improving quality and speed on LoCoMo.

name: unclutter
description: WXT browser extension for Chrome/Chromium and Firefox that uses the Jev AI model (with your own Vercel AI Gateway or TypeSafe AI key) to hide nonessential page elements via reusable per-template rules cached locally, with manual or on-visit analysis and pause/resume controls.

name: dify-plugin-typesafe-ai
description: A Dify Tool plugin for TypeSafe AI that provides Yes/No binary judgments with a tunable threshold and an Evaluate action batching typed noul/choice/score questions, exposing decisions, probabilities, and token usage as workflow variables over HTTPS to api.typesafe.ai.

name: jevmetrics
description: `jevmetrics` is an experimental OpenTelemetry Collector connector that asynchronously calls TypeSafe's Jev model to score metric instruments' operational value from their metadata, then applies cached, threshold-based keep/drop policy to annotate or filter metrics before export.

name: oxlint-plugin-jev
description: An oxlint plugin that turns plain-English yes/no questions about functions, calls, JSX elements, or whole files into lint rules—TypeSafe Jev returns a probability per match and reports an error at your configured cutoff, with per-file batching, answer caching, and CI fail/skip controls.

name: system-one-sdk
description: System One SDK is a modular TypeScript toolkit for typed decisions over shared state, providing an evaluate client, choice/score/boolean question types, pluggable transports and hosted, LLM, local ONNX, and browser WebGPU adapters, plus batching, policies, and evaluation harnesses.

name: jev-ai-sdk-form-router
description: A Next.js 16/React 19 example app that uses Jev with AI SDK 7 to route three form types (leads, contact, issue reports) to the right team, falling back to openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast when Jev's confidence drops below 95%, plus editable samples, routing stats, and optional Resend email delivery.

name: jev-desktop
description: Jev Desktop is a Codex plugin that keeps a bounded decision loop inside the existing Computer Use runtime—selecting one operation and compatible UI target per scoped TypeSafe request—so browser tab and native macOS app automation avoids per-click round-trips while Codex retains control of scope, permissions, prepared values, and verification.

name: jev-slot-machine
description: A local Node/Python tool that runs Jev on a slot machine—autonomously betting, leaving to spend winnings, buying items, resuming statefully, exposing CLI controls and a browser view—and logs every decision with option probabilities to JSONL for analysis.

name: joxide
description: joxide is a zsh plugin that layers TypeSafe Jev semantic ranking on top of zoxide's directory index, so `j` can jump to projects by natural-language description or visit date while exact name matching, `z` commands, and local-only mode still work.

name: sqlite-jev
description: sqlite-jev is a SQLite loadable extension and Python package adding natural-language predicates, classification, and scoring to SQL via TypeSafe Jev, including a batched `jev_rows` virtual table joinable by rowid, scalar functions, connection-local caching, and spend guards.

name: ai-elo-ranker
description: AI Elo Ranker is a FastAPI/asyncio tournament engine that ranks large text datasets via pairwise LLM-judged duels, using Swiss-system matchmaking to cut O(N²) comparisons to ~O(N log N), position-bias randomization, dynamic K-factor Elo scoring, SQLite persistence, and a real-time WebSocket dashboard with live leaderboards and match metrics.

name: youtube-sponsor-detection
description: A Chrome extension and companion web app that detect sponsor reads in YouTube videos using TypeSafe's Jev model over transcripts or live audio (via Deepgram), auto-skipping them with code-controlled timestamps and confidence thresholds so model uncertainty never cuts into actual content.

name: jev-search
description: A Chrome MV3 extension that performs semantic in-page search by natural-language description, using TypeSafe's Jev model via the Noul primitive to score each candidate word against page sentences and highlight only matching terms (e.g., "apple" for "food items") with Cmd+F-style navigation, keeping API keys in the background service worker.

name: TheOnlyArtz.github.io
description: A Hebrew/RTL React single-page app that ranks the 17 Knesset-26 party lists against a user's free-text ideology via a Supabase Edge Function scoring their verbatim manifestos, backed by local axis-vector analysis and a live public aggregate-stats board refreshed every 30 seconds.

name: jev-autopilot
description: A Three.js 3D drone simulator where TypeSafe's Jev model autonomously pilots a drone from pad A to pad B across a procedurally generated city: code builds plain-language situation reports, Jev answers six typed stick/landing questions with calibrated probabilities, and code converts the answers into stick deflections.

name: jev-form-filler-extension
description: A Chrome MV3 side-panel extension that scans web form fields, asks the Jev API to match each field against candidate values built from locally stored personal details, validates picks via confidence thresholds, then fills the page only when you click "Fill selected."

name: jimothy
description: Jimothy is a CLI plus Node.js and browser SDK that trains small, fast local classifiers from Jev-compatible task definitions and labeled or teacher-generated examples, offering calibrated predictions, evaluation, and offline inference via TF-IDF or MiniLM backends.

name: demo-expanso-jev
description: Demos pairing Expanso Edge pipelines with TypeSafe's Jev: routine log lines are fingerprinted and archived without model calls while ambiguous records get severity, team and routing judgments (with hold-and-release on outage), plus a live Kubernetes pod-label workflow.

name: Gambler-Jev
description: A localhost Flask blackjack game where an AI companion, Jev, reads the table after each deal and shows HIT/STAND/DOUBLE percentages, exact bust chance, and a plain-language recommendation via a TypeSafe API call, falling back to math-only basic strategy without a key.

name: jev-test
description: Benchmark harness and results for a pipeline where a dedicated judge model (TypeSafe's Jev) makes every decision a small local model is bad at, evaluated on 500 SimpleQA questions, plus `harness/audit.py` for auditing any judge's confidence scores via AUROC and gate mobility.

name: jev-align
description: A CLI/MCP/programmable verifier that scores every LLM response or agent plan on calibrated alignment heads (sycophancy, deception, overreach, sneaking, etc.) in ~800ms for ~$0.003, returning auditable probabilities and pass/flag/block verdicts enforceable via CI exit codes.

name: LLM2Jev
description: LLM2Jev turns local language models into Jev-style structured decision models, extracting Choice/Score/Noul probabilities from prefill logits without token-by-token decoding, with order-independent candidate scoring, multimodal inputs, SGLang prefix-cache reuse, and a System One–compatible API.

name: jev-gpt
description: jev-gpt generates text using jev—a model that only answers typed questions with probabilities—by hierarchically querying word type, WordNet category, embedding-clustered word groups, then the word, plus a final ranking pass (~400 calls, ~90 seconds, ~2 cents per prompt).

name: is-jeven
description: is-jeven is a joke TypeScript/JavaScript package exposing an async `isEven(num, options?)` function that calls TypeSafe AI's Jev model to determine whether an integer is even, supporting API-key override and AbortSignal cancellation.

name: rspamd-jev
description: rspamd-jev is an experimental, disabled-by-default Rspamd plugin that asynchronously sends sampled eligible mail to TypeSafe's Jev API for zero-score shadow evaluation—optionally paired with GPT verdicts—so operators can compare spam-classification quality without affecting delivery decisions.

name: mcp-jev
description: A minimal MCP server exposing a `jev_decide` tool that lets Cursor, Claude Code, and other MCP clients evaluate a `state` against typed yes/no, choice, and score questions via TypeSafe's Jev fast classifier, returning structured probabilities and answers over stdio or HTTP from a Docker container.

name: jev-plays-starcraft-2
description: An experimental StarCraft II harness where the Jev LLM makes every probabilistic gameplay decision via the game API while Python handles observation, validation, and transport, with commit-triggered policy hot-reloads, mission sequencing, JSONL decision logging, and a soft dollar spending cap.

name: jev-mac-voice
description: Jev Mac Voice is a local macOS Electron app that lets you control your Mac through natural spoken English conversations using the OpenAI Realtime API, combining React UI, native accessibility automation, optional screen sharing, and approval-gated actions.

name: jev-visual
description: A runnable Apple Silicon project for learning vision-language inference with Qwen3.5-0.8B via MLX, answering multiple questions per image by scoring candidate logits over shared multimodal context instead of autoregressive generation, with a local UI, CLI, HTTP API, demos, and benchmarks.

name: OpenWhisper
description: OpenWhisper is a cross-platform desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux that provides hotkey-driven dictation, audio-file transcription, and meeting capture with live dashboards using local speech models (Whisper, Parakeet, Qwen3-ASR, Moonshine) or the OpenAI API, plus AI text cleanup, searchable history, and export.

name: KaLM-Ultrafast
description: KaLM-Ultrafast is a local, CPU-runnable Chrome browser agent that loops observe-decide-act using the KaLM-Jev Nano reranker to choose grounded actions from indexed page elements, with a live inspector exposing every model decision plus freshness and occlusion guards that validate targets before execution.

name: SystemOneHarness
description: SystemOneHarness is a Python harness that turns a System One decision model into an agent loop by observing an environment, compiling its finite declared action space into typed questions, gating each model decision by confidence thresholds, executing the chosen action, and recording complete traces—with pluggable process, MCP, and browser environments plus a UHP-conformant server.

name: jev-skill-suggester
description: jev-skill-suggester is a Python CLI (also packaged as a Codex skill) that uses TypeSafe Jev to recommend relevant skills from those already installed, helping you pick the right capability for a task, with bilingual docs and live examples.

name: jev-file-search
description: jev-file-search is a Python CLI that finds local files by content: a model triages filenames, types, and short text previews, then reads deeper only into uncertain files, keeping natural-language searches like "find subscription receipts, not credit top-ups" fast and cheap.

name: typesafe-ai-playground
description: A zero-install Python playground serving a local three-panel dashboard for running 110 editable example scenarios — games, dilemmas, reasoning challenges, and practical use cases — through the TypeSafe API, with A/B comparisons, matched bias checks, typed noul/choice/score results, and run export.

name: jev-x-spam-filter
description: A Chrome extension that collapses spam replies (crypto shilling, porn solicitation, copy-paste bot floods) under X/Twitter status pages into expandable notices, combining local pattern rules with the typesafe-ai/jev evaluation model on Vercel AI Gateway for uncertain cases, with adjustable sensitivity.

name: jev-skils
description: A Claude Code skill that teaches agents to integrate TypeSafe's Jev System One model into JS/TS projects via noul/choice/score typed-decision primitives, with SDK/API references, a copyable retry wrapper, a runnable ticket-router demo, and confidence-gated routing patterns.

name: jev-engineering
description: Jev-gate screens every AI coding agent tool call through layered hard rules, an allowlist, and a fast decision model returning allow/ask/deny in ~400ms for ~$0.00002, with observe/guard/enforce modes, log-based calibration, a 300-call attack kit, and MCP support.

name: TerraBlind
description: A tModLoader mod exposing Terraria perception, pathfinding, building, and combat primitives over 152 HTTP endpoints, wired into a `/start` pipeline that autonomously runs a fresh world to killing the Wall of Flesh, plus a Jev model-driven boss-fighting layer.

name: jul
description: JuL is an offline MLX drop-in for the TypeSafe (Jev) Python SDK that answers typed decisions (Choice, Noul, Score) on Apple Silicon by comparing embedding vectors instead of generating tokens, yielding calibrated classifications in 64–273 ms, plus contexts and autotune heads.

name: jev-oasis
description: A fork of the CAMEL-AI OASIS social simulation engine that cuts LLM API costs by routing deterministic agent actions (liking, scrolling, following) through TypeSafe Jev's fast, low-cost System 1 router and invoking an LLM only for generative actions like posts and comments, reducing API calls ~67%.

name: jev-agent-skill-router
description: A Python CLI and library that routes a request to one skill in a catalogue—or abstains via no-skill or review—using batched TypeSafe Jev judgements, returning typed decisions with probabilities, confidence, latency and token usage for skill selection at scale without executing skills.

name: Typesafe_chess_eval
description: A tool evaluating typesafe AI chess performance, revealing that the model plays poorly — frequently calling draws in heavily unbalanced positions and assigning low loss probability even when a side is actually losing — suggesting it was not optimized for structured games like chess.

name: n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai
description: An n8n community node exposing the TypeSafe AI System One API as workflow operations—yes/no probabilities, one-of-N choices, ordered-level scores, batched multi-question evaluation, and model listing—returning calibrated probabilities that workflows can branch on without prompt engineering.

name: Jev-Desktop
description: Jev Desktop lets AI agents operate Windows applications through MCP or CLI, autonomously executing bounded tasks locally—observing windows, choosing controls, typing text—then returning the result or a help request instead of a model turn per click.

name: typesafe-mario
description: TypeSafe Mario is a Python harness that lets TypeSafe's Jev model play Super Mario Bros. by parsing emulator RAM into structured JSON describing Mario's motion, hazards, terrain, and timing, then translating the model's Choice/Noul/Score judgments into controller inputs, with a live telemetry dashboard and per-decision JSONL logging.

name: subcortex
description: subcortex is a local daemon that adds a fast typed-decision layer to 29 terminal coding agents—via a hosted API (~250 ms) or a private local model (~10 ms)—to flag simple prompts, trim unneeded tool output, and preserve context across compaction.

name: skills
description: A collection of agent skills for building with TypeSafe's System One API, giving coding agents reusable guidance and workflows that make it easier to integrate and work with the API correctly.

name: jev-bot
description: Jev-bot is a public hosted web app and loopback CLI that evaluates a user-described idea against a complete exported library of 466 Jev use cases and findings, returning a proposed visual workflow, illustrative inputs with copyable Jev JSON, external evidence links, and per-stage token and cost estimates.

name: jevfill
description: Jevfill is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension that autofills web forms by sending field context plus locally stored plain-text notes to the Jev API to match fields against note lines with a configurable confidence threshold, highlighting results for review while never sending or filling password and payment fields.

name: Jev-MongoDB
description: Jev-MongoDB is a real-time customer-care triage demo where MongoDB change streams trigger TypeSafe's Jev model to return four typed judgments (category, sentiment, urgency, safety) in ~300 ms, then push verdicts to live dashboards via SSE with no polling.

name: logjev
description: LogJev is a Node.js/TypeScript server that turns any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint returning `top_logprobs` into a structured decision API, yielding full probability distributions for choice, score, and noul questions over text, image, and audio inputs.

name: dsh-jev-guard
description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that hard-intercepts every bash/pwsh command before execution via unoverridable offline rules, a read-only pre-screen, and a ~300ms Jev yes/no semantic check, returning allow/revise/block/escalate to prevent irreversible data loss.

name: jev-java
description: jev-java is an idiomatic Java SDK for integrating the TypeSafe AI Jev System One decision engine, letting Java applications invoke and manage AI-powered decisions through a natural, Java-native API.

name: syft-listening
description: Syft Listening is a database-free Rails web app that uses browser Web Speech API transcription and a server-side Jev proxy to turn finalized speech into live, toggleable insights for factual claims, specificity, complexity, grammar, emotion, and speech habits without storing API keys.

name: typed-decisions-shadow-layer
description: A shadow CRM decision layer that turns inbound WhatsApp/Telegram/email messages into typed, confidence-scored outputs (intent, division, urgency, human-handoff and lead probabilities) via TypeSafe's Jev or a JSON-forced local model, logging decisions without sending.

name: clojev
description: CloJev is an unofficial Clojure SDK for the TypeSafe System One API that sends state and typed questions (noul, choice, score), lists models, and returns validated data with retries, Retry-After support, structured errors, and JVM or Jolt HTTP backends on a portable .cljc core.

name: SemIf
description: SemIf adds semantic if-condition evaluation backed by open models running locally on a home NVIDIA RTX 3090, enabling meaning-based branching without depending on a hosted model service.

name: TypeSafeAI.Net
description: TypeSafeAI.Net is a community .NET SDK (net8.0/net10.0, AOT-safe) for the TypeSafe AI System One API, providing typed Noul/Choice/Score questions that return calibrated probabilities, plus Polly retries, DI, OpenTelemetry diagnostics, and Microsoft.Extensions.AI middleware for guardrails, intent routing, tool calls, and evaluation.

name: necro
description: Necro runs Qwen3.5-0.8B locally to score candidate answers, yes/no questions, and ordered choices directly with probabilities—no explanation or JSON parsing—served via CLI or a TypeSafe-compatible HTTP API, using base, LoRA, or exported merged weights.

name: jev-codex-router
description: A Codex Router plugin that classifies every turn with Jev and routes it to the cheapest capable model (luna/sol/astra) at adaptive reasoning depth—cutting cost ~60% vs all-frontier—with fail-open fallback, dry-mode substitutes, and local decision logs.

name: JevPixelArt
description: A Next.js tool that generates pixel art by asking the Jev model one Score question per channel per pixel through the TypeSafe API, sharpening the returned probability distributions into colors, and painting a live canvas via chunked, resumable browser-side requests with PNG/JSON export.

name: typesafe-skill-router
description: An opt-in, stdlib-only skill router for Hermes Agent that uses TypeSafe (Jev) to name the single most relevant skill to load before each model call, costing roughly $0.001 per routed turn.

name: plausible-rooms
description: A Node.js harness that deterministically generates one-room fantasy-industrial scenes with seeded faults, has the Jev model judge each as a place via fixed questions, buckets verdicts under pre-registered rules, and renders auditable runs in local galleries.

name: jev-use
description: jev-use is a macOS voice-and-typed computer-use agent that reads the Accessibility tree instead of screenshots, lets an LLM pick each on-screen action, executes presses, typing, menus, scrolling and window arrangement, and verifies real effects in a loop until done.

name: jev-precheck
description: jev-precheck is an MCP proxy that forwards reads untouched but, before each write, fetches affected records and computes comparisons in code so Jev can flow, warn, or hold well-formed but wrong calls like duplicate payments or oversized credit notes.

name: system-one-adapter-python
description: Drop-in replacement for typesafe_sdk's `system_one` evaluation API backed by OpenAI/Anthropic LLMs instead of TypeSafe, enabling cost/speed/intelligence comparisons with sync/async clients, structured outputs, probability normalization, retries, and usage/debug telemetry.

name: jev-pr-judge
description: A web app, CLI, and GitHub Action that judges whether a pull request does what it claims, combining TypeSafe System One typed answers (scores, yes/no flags, verdict) with deterministic code facts and code-defined policy rules — cheap enough to gate every PR.

name: jev-korean-benchmark
description: A reproducible, frozen 100-question-per-cell evaluation measuring whether the TypeSafe Jev decision model degrades on Korean versus English across four public test sets (Belebele, PAWS-X, KorMedMCQA, MedQA), reporting accuracy with uncertainty intervals, input-order sensitivity, latency, cost, and a mainstream-LLM comparison.

name: typesafe21
description: A terminal-based blackjack simulator pitting random, basic-strategy, and AI players against identical starting hands, using TypeSafe's System One Choice and Score primitives for autonomous decisions and balance-based bet sizing informed by full shoe and counting state.

name: spring-ai-model-router
description: A Spring Boot app that asks Jev via the Spring AI TypeSafe starter to classify each prompt into one of four capability tiers (luna to astra), then routes it to the cheapest sufficient OpenAI model and returns the answer with the routing decision and confidence.

name: jev-review
description: jev-review splits a diff into per-file chunks, triages each through Jev via the Vercel AI Gateway, and emits a JSON report — full diffs for flagged files, one-line verdicts for clean ones — so review agents spend tokens only on risky changes.

name: reaper
description: Reaper is a CLI semantic linter for coding agents that checks Git diffs or codebases and emits deterministic text/JSON diagnostics for semantic problems ordinary linters miss, like narrating comments, shallow abstractions, silent fallbacks, weakened assertions, and scope creep.

name: seems-lang
description: Seems is a Python superset language where `if` conditions can be plain-English judgments answered by the TypeSafe Jev API, with three-valued yes/no/unsure logic, lazy batched requests, caching, and line-preserving translation to ordinary Python.

name: jev-notion
description: jev-notion is a macOS SwiftUI app and CLI that fills Notion database properties with calibrated AI judgments, detecting row edits in ≤2s at ~$0.00004/row, routing uncertain entries to a review queue, with 8-language UI and Keychain-secured credentials.

name: purelink
description: A browser extension that scores LinkedIn posts for AI authorship using a lightweight decision model answering 17 weighted questions instead of an LLM, flags engagement/curiosity/rage bait, and offers an on-demand fact-checker that annotates claims in place with sourced verdicts.

name: jev-shogi
description: jev-shogi makes TypeSafe's judgment-only Jev model play shogi by passing all legal moves as probability-scored choices in one inference (no search engine), and ships v2/v3 lookahead variants, Fairy-Stockfish match results, KIF/mp4 game records, and calibration and replay-rendering scripts.

name: skillranker
description: SkillRanker is a standalone Rust CLI that uses TypeSafe.ai’s Jev to evaluate live agent context against available skills, recommend the most suitable next-step procedure, abstain when none fits, and provide inspectable explanations, safeguards, and local feedback.

name: jevis
description: Jevis is a Dart package for Flutter's integration_test framework that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to drive UI tests: you register available actions, state a goal and action budget, and the model observes the current screen, picks the next action, and evaluates whether the goal is reached.

name: typesafe-sdk-go
description: A zero-dependency Go client for the TypeSafe AI API that returns statically-typed answers (probabilities, classifications, rubric scores) to named questions in one request, with pre-network validation, typed errors, retries, and per-call overrides.

name: JevNQL
description: JevNQL compiles natural-language data questions into typed JevIR plans that route deterministic arithmetic to Apache DataFusion and only meaning judgments to the Jev semantic model, ordering filters and top-k first so minimal rows reach costly model calls, cutting token cost.

name: jev-chatbot
description: An experimental chatbot harness that turns TypeSafe’s non-generative Jev choice model into a next-word or reply selector over 30k words, with browser and Node CLI interfaces, seven comparison modes, cached embedding-built trees, and measured speed, cost, and quality tradeoffs.

name: TypeAR
description: TypeAR is a constrained-decoding client for SGLang-served open autoregressive LLMs that yields type-safe outputs (single-token enum/boolean choices, bounded numeric values, free text) via sequential or prefix-cached batch execution, with optional thinking, sampling, and per-choice probabilities.

name: is-odd-jev
description: A zero-dependency Node.js library and CLI that checks whether a number is odd by querying the Jev "System One" model (via TypeSafe API or Vercel AI Gateway), returning the model's calibrated probability rather than a parsed string so callers can threshold confidence and escalate uncertain cases.

name: jev-router
description: An open-source LiteLLM-based proxy that exposes an OpenAI-compatible `jev-router` model id and routes each request to an eligible pool model—filtered by vision, tool, and output-length requirements—using TypeSafe's Jev model when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set or a local cheapest-eligible fallback otherwise.

name: book-aurora

name: Armada
description: Armada is a control plane for orchestrating AI coding captains across git repositories with isolated worktrees, durable mission records, gated pipelines, tiered routing, and REST/MCP/WebSocket access to dispatch, monitor, review, and land parallel work.

description: An opencode plugin that replaces lossy LLM-summary context compaction with Jev scoring: once session context occupancy crosses a configurable threshold, every tool call and result is individually kept verbatim, truncated, or deleted based on scored relevance.

name: typesafe-sdk-js
description: JavaScript/TypeScript SDK for TypeSafe AI that provides a `TypeSafeClient` for sending state and structured questions (e.g., `choice`) to `systemOne` and receiving type-inferred answers, distributed as ESM, CommonJS, and TypeScript declarations for Node.js 20+.

name: typesafe-sdk-ruby
description: An unofficial Ruby SDK for the TypeSafe AI API that evaluates state against noul, choice, and score questions, returning typed answers with probabilities and confidence, with retries, timeouts, cancellation, and an error hierarchy for classification, ranking, and routing.

name: jev-reflex
description: jev-reflex is a macOS interaction engine that combines local MediaPipe hand tracking, offline Vosk partial speech, and window geometry with confidence-gated Jev typed decisions via OpenRouter to target, snap, resize, and control windows through gestures and voice, visualized on a token-authenticated Next.js dashboard.

name: jev-chat-JARVIS-windows

name: jev-weekend-shopping-chrome
description: A Chrome extension (v0.4.6, Chrome 137+, MIT, unpacked install) that overlays a "PASS" stamp on Taobao and JD.com product images whose items, shops, or brands are AI-guessed via a user-supplied TypeSafe API key to lack two-day weekends, with an on/off toggle and live stats.

name: metis
description: Metis is a dependency-free Python 3.10+ library, CLI, and GitHub Action that uses TypeSafe’s Jev model to triage new GitHub issues, apply confident labels, request missing details, and safely skip uncertain or changed cases.

name: jev-search
description: A self-hostable Cloudflare Workers app that turns plain-language requests into Search1API queries across web and vertical engines, then streams Jev-scored, URL-merged links and snippets with visible relevance, editable source/time filters, caching, and per-IP rate limits.

name: magi-system-on-jev
description: A web app recreating Neon Genesis Evangelion's MAGI system using TypeSafe AI's Jev "System One" model, where three independent sage agents evaluate a question and reach a verdict via majority vote over calibrated probabilities, with a live CloudFront deployment and bilingual docs.

name: typesafe-mod
description: A Claude Code function hook that routes AskUserQuestion dialogs and per-prompt skill ranking to TypeSafe's Jev model, returning typed answers with probabilities and confidence scores so the agent can advise, auto-answer, or inject skill hints while failing open on any error.

name: youtube-focus

name: jev-rs

description: AutoJev-27B is a Qwen3.8-27B–based multimodal decision model that returns calibrated probabilities over supplied choices in one forward pass per question, served via a TypeSafe-compatible API and browser playground, achieving 84.60% accuracy with lower ECE and Brier scores than its base model.

name: jev-ultrafast

name: typesafe-ai-ruby
description: A dependency-free Ruby client for the TypeSafe System One API that sends state plus typed questions (yes/no Nouls, multi-option Choices, ordinal Scores) to the Jev model and returns structured answers with probabilities and confidence scores, plus retries, instrumentation, and per-call configuration.

description: Benchmark suite evaluating Jev 1.13.0 zero-shot inference via the TypeSafe API against frozen supervised checkpoints and a local NLI baseline on five pinned benchmarks (BANKING77, CLINC150, HWU64, SST-2, STS-B), with resumable runs and paired-bootstrap comparisons.

name: security-sandbox-jev
description: security-sandbox-jev is a sandboxed testbed that puts a policy-enforcing gateway between AI agents and a fake 50-person company's API, using the Jev classifier to score every action (allow/block/hold) based on agent identity, verified initiator, and planted adversarial traps, with audit logging and a live bench UI.

name: jev_benchmark
description: A benchmark comparing the Jev routing model with open-source alternatives on 100 multi-turn enterprise RAG agent cases, scoring each turn's route, scope-change, mode, and restriction decisions plus latency to reveal accuracy and predictability tradeoffs.

name: jevspin
description: Browser app that visualizes TypeSafe's Jev judgment model solving a Rubik's cube through menu-based choices, offering guided and discovery modes, a random-picker control, benchmark script, keyless mock backend, and Cloudflare Workers deployment.

description: An Emacs global minor mode that reranks ddskk Japanese conversion candidates by sending surrounding context, reading, and okurigana to TypeSafe AI's Jev evaluation model (via Vercel AI Gateway or the direct TypeSafe API) and ordering candidates by their returned probabilities.

description: A local Node.js demo that executes a Mermaid flowchart subset as ticket-routing logic, requesting typed Choice and Score judgments from Jev via `@typesafe-ai/sdk` and highlighting the computed route in the browser, with a fixture-backed Preview mode that works without an API key.

description: typesafe-playground provides three Dockerized interactive demos—Decision Lab, Jev Driving Lab, and a Fable implementation—that expose TypeSafe Jev's real API-driven judgments, sensor inputs, and driving decisions via inspectable localhost interfaces.

name: hx
description: Hx watches a clinician type or dictate a note, opens the questions that note calls for, ticks them off against what was actually written, and surfaces what remains undocumented — quoting only clauses and values from the note, never generating text.

name: plz
description: A Rust daemon for fish that intercepts commands before execution, sending them to TypeSafe's API for a verdict — allowing, prompting for confirmation (once/always/no), or denying — with a permanent SQLite cache keyed to command and context, an editable review prompt, on/off toggling, and usage/latency statistics.

name: livesignal
description: LiveSignal is a local, real-time livestream-chat intelligence system that runs live TypeSafe Jev decisions on every comment to surface, cluster, and rank genuine questions for creators, with typed signals, telemetry, and a reproducible 240-comment evaluation corpus.

name: jev-browser
description: jev-browser is an MCP/CLI/library automation layer where an LLM states one outcome and values, Jev picks the element/action/status, and Playwright executes it—cutting page-context tokens while handling complex UIs and flagging blocked, ambiguous, or irreversible steps.

name: feed-lens
description: Feed Lens is an open-source Chrome extension that labels Weibo, Threads, and X posts with customizable topic and expression-style tags, classified via your TypeSafe API key using editable label descriptions, with per-platform dictionaries and JSON import/export.
